24/2022FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Fahey and Sally Hughes
  1. THAT Council note the report on the urgent works required for the Howlong Water Treatment and Reticulation network;
  2. THAT the design, approval, and tender documentation be prepared for;
    a) A 375 mm rising main from the treatment plant to the Read Street Howlong Water Tower,
    b) The refurbishment of the existing water tower,
    c ) An additional 2.5 megalitre water tower to be constructed in the Read Street Howlong road reserve,
    d) A new 375 mm trunk water main to be constructed along Townsend Street Howlong, from Victoria Street to Kennedy Street Howlong,
    e) For other ancillary works, and a road closure for Read Street between Hawkins Street and Pell Street, and minor modification works to the treatment plant.
  3. THAT estimates for the works be finalised and referred to the budget preparations for 2022/2023;
  4. THAT subject to suitable funding avenues being proposed, the works be prioritised in the draft Long Term Financial Plan and Delivery Program for 22/23 and 23/24; and
  5. THAT delegation be granted to the General Manager to negotiate the closure of the Read Street Howlong Road Reserve between Hawkins Street and Pell Street, for the provision of the second water tower in Howlong, and that the resulting lot created via the required subdivision, be defined as Operational land in accordance with The Local Government Act 1979.

Councillor David Longley returned to the meeting at 10.10 am.

112/2022FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Fahey and Shaun Whitechurch
  1. THAT the onsite Carparking required by table 4.1 of Corowa Development Control Plan 2012 be varied by 3% to permit 29 onsite parking space for the development as the overall development in is the public interest due to the provision of medical and allied health services to the region; and
  2. THAT Council grant development consent to Development Application No. 2022/480 for Medical Centre and Signage on Lot 18, DP 1184334, addressed as 53-55 Guy Street, Corowa dated 21 February 2022 and described in details accompanying the application under Section 4.16 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act, 1979 and subject to the following conditions.

Conditions of consent

1. CONSTRUCTION CERTIFICATE:  A construction certificate is required to be issued prior to commencement of any building work. 
2. LONG SERVICE LEVY:  Payment of the Building and Construction Industry Long Service Levy will be required prior to the issue of a Construction Certificate.
3. HOURS OF WORK:  Hours for construction may only be carried out between 7.00am and 5.00pm on Monday to Saturday and no construction is to be carried out at any time on a Sunday or Public Holiday.
Hours of operation of the development are to be 7.00am to 6.00pm Monday to Friday and 9.00am to 12 noon Saturday.
4. SITE SIGN:  A sign must be erected in a prominent position on any site on which building work, subdivision or demolition work is being carried out:

a. Showing the name, address and telephone number of the principal certifying authority for the work, and
b. Showing the name of the principal contractor (if any) for any building work and a telephone number on which that person may be contacted outside working hours, and
c. Stating that unauthorized entry to the site is prohibited.
Any such sign is to be maintained while the building work, subdivision work or demolition work is being carried out, but must be removed when the work has been completed.

5. ON-SITE TOILET FACILITIES are to be provided prior to the commencement of any works.
6. OCCUPATION OF BUILDING:  The building is not to be used or occupied until all conditions of Development Consent have been complied with and a Certificate of Occupancy issued.
7. BCA:  the work must be carried out in accordance with the requirements of the Building Code of Australia.
8. DEVELOPER CONTRIBUTIONS

a. Developer contributions will be payable in accordance with Federation Councils Development Contributions Plan 2019, under Section 7.12 Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979. A copy of the document is available on Federation Councils website.

9. PROTECTION OF PUBLIC PLACE:  If the building or demolition work is likely to affect pedestrian or vehicle traffic in a public place a hoarding or fence is to be provided.
10. EROSION CONTROL:  If the site conditions require it, approved methods of preventing erosion control movement of the soil must be provided.  Adequate provisions must be made for drainage.
11. EXCAVATIONS AND BACKFILLING:  All excavations and backfilling associated with the erection or demolition of a building must be executed safely and in accordance with appropriate professional standards.  All works are to be protected to prevent them from being dangerous to life or property.
12. USE OF PUBLIC LAND:  The naturestrip/footpath/roadway shall not be used for the storage of building materials i.e. sand, bricks, timber etc.  The public land outside the property is to be maintained in its original condition to enable safe pedestrian access past the site at all times.
13. ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT:  The activities shall be undertaken in such a way as to not interfere with the amenity of the locality by reason of the emission of noise, vibration, smell, fumes, smoke, vapour, steam, ash, soot, dust, waste water, waste products or grit, oil or otherwise.
14. ADVICE – WORK WITHIN A RESERVE PERMIT:  For all works on the footpath/naturestrip or roadway, please contact Council’s Engineering Department on (02) 6033 8999 to obtain the necessary permits and construction standards.
15. PLUMBING:  Plumbing and drainage installation and alteration shall be carried out in accordance with the provision of the NSW Code of Practice for Plumbing and Drainage which adopts the National Plumbing and Drainage Code AS3500, with NSW variations.
16. SANITARY PLUMBING AND DRAINAGE:  All sanitary plumbing and drainage work shall only be carried out by a licensed plumber and drainer and no work is to be covered over or concealed from view until it has been inspected and approved by the Approval Authority.
17. REQUIREMENTS FOR H1, H2 and E SITES: Drains attached to or emerging from underneath the building shall incorporate flexible joints immediately outside the footing and commencing within 1 metre of the building perimeter. This requirement applies to all stormwater and sanitary plumbing drains and discharge pipes (AS2870, Section 5.6.4).
18. PLUMBING AND DRAINAGE APPROVAL: Prior to commencement of works, submit to the Council for approval the prescribed application to carry out plumbing and drainage works.
19. ACCESS TO PREMISES LEGISLATION: The owner of the building shall ensure that, when completed, the works comply with the provisions and requirements of the Disability (Access to Premises – Buildings) Standards 2010.
20. ANTI-DISCRIMINATION LEGISLATION:  This development has been assessed in accordance with the relevant building laws and it remains the responsibility of the builder to ensure compliance with other laws, including anti-discrimination legislation.
21. IDENTIFICATION OF FACILITIES, SERVICES, FEATURES:  Clear and legible braille and tactile signage complying with specification D3.6 and incorporating the international symbol of access, or deafness or other symbol in accordance with AS1428.1 must identify each:

(a) Sanitary facility
(b) Hearing augmentation system
(c) Accessible entrance
(d) The path of travel from the principle entrance to these facilities.

(See BCA D3.6 and Specification D3.6).
22. FINAL FIRE SAFETY CERTIFICATE:  Upon completion of the building the owner shall cause the Council to be furnished with a Certificate in relation to each fire safety measure included in the Schedule attached to the Construction Certificate.
23. DRIVEWAYS:  All vehicular movements to and from the premises shall be made in a forward direction only.
24. EXTERNAL LIGHTING - The applicant shall ensure that lighting of the carpark and building surrounds is installed such that no glare nuisance occurs to adjoining neighbours and sufficient lighting is provided at all times that the building is occupied such that the safety of users entering and
25. VEHICULAR ACCESS ON SITE - The applicant shall ensure that:

a. The swept path of the largest vehicle entering and exiting the subject site and manoeuvrability through the site is in accordance with AS 2890.2-2002 "Off-street commercial vehicle facilities" and to Council's satisfaction. For road safety reasons the internal layout of the development shall be designed to allow all vehicles to enter and exit the subject site in a forward direction and not be required to reverse onto the adjoining road reserve; and
b. Any access driveway to the development is to be constructed so that the formed vehicle path rises to the level of the footpath along the frontage of the site and not have the footpath step down onto the driveway. As a minimum the driveway shall be sealed from the edge of the seal of the carriageway to and within the trafficable areas.
c. LINE MARKING - INTERNAL VEHICULAR MANOEUVRING - The applicant shall ensure that aisles, parking areas and loading areas shall be maintained clear of obstruction and used exclusively for the purposes of vehicle access, parking and loading respectively. This is to provide for the ease of circulation of vehicles within the development site. These areas shall not be used for the storage of goods or waste receptacles or any other purpose.
d. VEHICLE LOADING - PEDESTRIAN MOVEMENTS - Facilities are to be provided to facilitate safe pedestrian movements throughout the site. Traffic calming devices are to be installed to minimise conflict between pedestrians and vehicles within the site. Pedestrian crossing stripes are not to be installed as these resemble pedestrian crossings on the road and create confusion as to who has priority.

26. OFF STREET PARKING - The applicant shall ensure that all off street parking areas are designed and installed in accordance with AS 2890.1-2004 "Off Street Parking", AS 2890.2-2002 "Off street commercial vehicle facilities" and the Austroads Guide to Traffic management Part 11: Parking.
27. LANDSCAPING, FENCING & SIGNAGE – Any landscaping, fencing or signage to be provided within the site or along the boundary with any adjoining road reserve is to be designed and maintained to provide safe sight distance to pedestrians for motorists entering and exiting the site to minimise conflict in accordance with AS2890.1-2004 “Off-street car parking”.
28. DAMAGE OR DISTURBANCE IN ROAD RESERVE – Any damage or disturbance to the road reserve is to be restored to match surrounding landform in accordance with Council requirements. Any redundant vehicular access points to the subject site from Federation Avenue shall be removed and the road reserve and kerb and gutter reinstated to match the surrounding roadside landform in accordance with Council requirements.
29. PRIOR TO ISSUE OF A CONSTRUCTION CERTIFICATE the applicant shall:

a. Submit and have approved by Council a Landscape Plan that clearly indicates the proposed location and species of all plants and details the means by which establishment and maintenance of all plantings will be effected. This may include such things as automatic irrigation systems, mulching etc.
b. A report by an appropriately qualified person which details the requirements and installation necessary to comply with Part J of the National Construction Code (NCC).
c. Provide and have approved a Water Supply Plan. The plan must include computations and must show details as listed in Council's Engineering Guidelines for Subdivisions and Development Standards. The plan must address achievement of the following minimums;

i. Peak instantaneous demand of 0.15 litres per second per tenement at minimum allowable service pressures of 200kPa (20m head); and
ii. Minimum supply head of 16m is to be achieved at any fire hydrant within the reticulation system when drawing 11 litres per second from the individual hydrant and meeting instantaneous demand of 0.10 litres per second per tenement throughout the system.
iii. Hydraulic designs and calculations that confirm compliance with pressure requirements for Fire Services (hydrants and hose reels).

d. Provide Stormwater runoff calculations and designs that demonstrate suitability of the existing infrastructure to accept anticipated flows.
e. Submit and obtain approval for a Construction Waste Management Plan that details all waste expected to be generated, details the means of and location for disposal and any recycling of products.
f. Submit and obtain approval for a Construction Phase Traffic Management Plan which details all measures to be implemented to ensure the safe and efficient movement of traffic on and off the site. The plan shall demonstrate that suitable provision is available on site for all vehicles associated with the construction of the development to alleviate any need to park within, or load/unload from any road reserve. The storage of any material within the road reserve of Guy Street is not permitted. Appropriate signage and fencing is to be installed and maintained to effect this requirement.
g. Submit details of and obtain separate approval for the proposed advertising structure.
h. Submit and obtain approval for a Drainage Discharge Plan. The plan shall contain computations and be drawn to scale with dimensions. The information submitted must show details listed in council's Engineering Guidelines for Subdivision and Development Standards and be designed in accordance with the requirements of the manual. The information and plan must include catchment details and computations demonstrating how the works on the land are to be drained and retarded for a maximum discharge rate no greater than pre-development flow for a 20% AEP storm event. NOTE: Stormwater runoff from the subject site onto the adjoining road reserve and private property is not permitted. Any access driveway is to be designed and constructed to prevent water from proceeding onto the carriageway of the adjoining road reserve.

30. SECTION 68 APPROVAL & TRADE WASTE APPROVAL - The applicant shall apply obtain approval under section 68 of the Local Government Act for discharge of trade waste and the installation of all sanitary plumbing and drainage. The Applicant must ensure that a valid Liquid Trade Waste Approval has been granted for the discharge of liquid trade waste to Council’s sewerage infrastructure.
31. PRIOR TO COMMENCEMENT OF CONSTRUCTION the applicant shall:

a. Provide an Identification Survey by a Registered Surveyor and peg the metes and bounds of the property. Pegs so installed shall be clearly identified and protected from damage or movement for the duration of the construction project.
b. Obtain a Road Opening Permit from Council's Engineering Department.

32. DURING CONSTRUCTION the applicant shall:

a. Provide a 24 hour telephone complaints "hotline" number and contact for the purpose of dealing with complaints and minimising disruption to adjoining residences and other neighbours. The details of this hotline shall be clearly displayed on a sign at the front of the building site for the duration of the construction phase.

33. PRIOR TO COMMENCEMENT OF THE RELEVANT WORK the applicant shall:

a. Separate approval shall be obtained for the proposed advertising structure.

34. PRIOR TO ISSUE OF AN OCCUPATION CERTIFICATE the applicant shall:

a. Certification by an appropriately qualified person confirming that the installations and requirements of the Part J Compliance Report have been provided/installed.
b. Confirmation of construction in accordance with the approved Drainage Discharge Plan shall be obtained from Council's Engineering Department.
c. The development must have a vehicular crossing constructed to the satisfaction of Federation Council and shall comply with the following:
Constructed at right angles to the road with any redundant crossings to be removed; and
Satisfactory clearances to any side-entry pit, power or telecommunications pole, manhole cover or marker or street tree. Any relocation, alteration or replacement required shall be in accordance with the requirements of the relevant Authority and shall be at the applicant's expense; and
Crossings shall be constructed of concrete and be generally in accordance with Federation Council's standard drawing SD409.

35. POST OCCUPATION/DURING USE the owner shall:

135/2022FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Gail Law and Aaron Nicholls

THAT Council resolve to decline to accept any tender in relation upon clause 178(3)(a) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 and cancel the proposal for the contract to construct a new Public Administration building as specified in RFT2021-161.

The Mayor asked that his vote against be recorded.

136/2022FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Gail Law and Aaron Nicholls
  1. THAT Council resolve to revise the scope of Stage 3 of the Corowa Saleyards Redevelopment Project to avoid the need for additional funding over and above the remaining project budget, and award contracts without the need for a further tender, in reliance upon section 55(3)(i) of the Local Government Act 1993, nothing the following extenuating circumstances:
    • Requirement to comply with the June 2022 timeline outlined in the Funding Deed;
    • The limited responses to the initial tender, resulting in an uncompetitive outcome;
    • Knowledge gained from the initial tender including awareness that a number of reputable local contractors did not submit tenders due to current commitments of workload; and
    • Challenges in sourcing building materials and securing building-trade contractors in the current market.
  2. THAT Council consider a further report providing proposed changes to scope of Stage 3 of the project at the May Ordinary Council meeting, with recommendation for Council to adopt the revised scope to secure administration building accommodation arrangements whereby the project can proceed in accordance with the requirements of the funding deed, including budget and timetable.

The Mayor asked that his vote against be recorded.

137/2022FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Gail Law and Aaron Nicholls

164/2022FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Longley and Andrew Kennedy
  1. THAT the shed constructed without consent at Lot 8, DP 184825, 44 Wanani Road, Mulwala be retained;
  2. THAT a building information certificate application be lodged prior to use of the shed;
  3. THAT an application for the use only of the shed be applied for and the application be notified to adjoining landowners. The use application is to address:

    2. That a landscaping plan be prepared to mitigate the impact on the neighbouring property to the east of the shed.

171/2022FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Fahey and David Longley
  1. THAT Council note the report on the Corowa Saleyards Redevelopment Project - Stage 3 Update;

  2. THAT Council seek a four month extension and an additional $400,000 from the NSW Government, to the current deadline of 30 June 2022, to have the funds committed for this element of the project, and seek the support of local member Justin Clancy MP, for the following reasons -
    a) to allow a more reasonable time for the market to respond to a new tender process that could also include alternative proposals being submitted;
    b) to allow the building element of this project to have the best possible chance of delivering on the original intent (including functionality/aesthetics/longevity/value for money),
    c) that this request is considered reasonable given Council has met all of the other funding deadlines thus far, including major contracts being in place for the roof, and civil and associated works, and
    d) that this request is also considered reasonable given the time that elapsed from the funding announcement to the time that Council finally had an agreed funding deed in place (approximately 6 months).

  3. THAT Council receive a further report at a future Council meeting once the NSW Government has responded to Councils request for additional funding and a 4 month extension to the project timeline.

221/2022FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Fahey and Andrew Kennedy
 THAT Council notes the report on the Rural Fire Services (RFS) assets;
  1. THAT Council writes to the local State Member(s) Mr Justin Clancy MP – Member for Albury, the Treasurer the Hon Matt Kean MP, Minister for Emergency Services and Resilience the Hon Stephanie Cook MP and the Minister for Local Government Wendy Tuckerman MP:
    1. Expressing Council’s objection to the NSW Government’s determination on ownership of Rural Fire Service assets;
    2. Advising of the impact of the Government’s position on Council finances of this accounting treatment;
    3. Informing that Council will not carry out RFS assets stocktakes on behalf of the NSW Government and will not record RFS assets in (Federation Council’s) financial statements;
    4. Calling on the NSW Government to take immediate action to permanently clear up inequities and inconsistencies around the accounting treatment of Rural Fire Service (RFS) assets by acknowledging that rural firefighting equipment is vested in, under the control of and the property of the RFS; and
    5. Amending s119 of the Rural Fires Act 1997 so that the effect is to make it clear that RFS assets are not the property of councils.
  2. THAT Council writes to the Shadow Treasurer Daniel Mookhey MLC, the Shadow Minister for Emergency Services Jihad Dib MP, the Shadow Minister for Local Government Greg Warren MP, the Greens Spokesperson for Local Government Jamie Parker MP and the leaders of the Shooters, Fishers and Farmers, Animal Justice and One Nation parties Robert Borsak MLC, Emma Hurst MLC and Mark Latham MLC:
    1. Advising Members of (Federation Council’s) position, including providing copies of correspondence to NSW Government Ministers; and
    2. Seeking Members’ commitments to support NSW Councils’ call to amend the Rural Fires Act 1997 as set out in correspondence.
  3. THAT Council writes to the Auditor General advising that notwithstanding any overtures of future qualified audits, it will not carry out RFS stocktakes on behalf of the NSW Government and will not record RFS assets in (Federation Council’s) financial statements, noting that the State Government’s own Local Government Accounting Code of Practice and Financial Reporting provides for councils to determine whether or not they record the RFS assets as council assets; 
  4. THAT Council promotes these messages via its digital and social media channels and via its networks;
  5. THAT Council re-affirms its complete support of and commitment to local RFS brigades noting that (Federation Council’s) action is entirely directed towards the NSW Government’s nonsensical position that rather than being owned and controlled by local brigades, RFS assets are somehow controlled by councils, which councils consider to be a cynical financial sleight of hand abdicating the NSW Government’s responsibilities at the cost of local communities; and 
  6. THAT Council affirms its support to Local Government NSW (LGNSW) and requests LGNSW continue advocating on Council’s behalf to get clarification finally from the State Government about the accounting treatment of RFS assets.

248/2022FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Longley and Sally Hughes
  1. THAT Council note the report on possible motions for the 2022 LGNSW Annual Conference; and
  2. THAT Council submit the following motions to the 2022 LGNSW Annual Conference:
  1. That the NSW Government allow for more general road grant allocations, such as varying the criteria for Fixing Local Roads and Fixing Country Roads grant programs, to not require them to be applied to a specific road, and allow the Councils to submit groups of roads, to allow the funds to be spread across a wider range of roads.
  2. That the NSW Government double the amount of funding currently received under the repair program and block grant for the next four years, to assist Councils address the backlog in regional roads.
  3. That the NSW Government work with Councils to develop consistent requirements for Councils to adopt Climate Adaptation Plans, and develop in consultation with Councils, a clear framework to allow the plans to be implemented, including clear conduits to Government (including Federal) funding programs.
  4. That the NSW Government develop a clear framework to allow Councils to work with the State Government, Industry in their Council areas who require housing, and other stakeholders, to allow Councils to develop housing strategies that have a clearer connection to outcomes, including funding programs.
  5. That the NSW Government allow Councils with adopted Growth Strategies and accompanying service plans and reflective Local Environmental Plans, to have access to a funding stream that assists Councils to fund network infrastructure and sewer and water plants (new/replacement or upgrades), to reflect the growing need for housing in rural and regional areas.

  1. THAT Ordinary Council Meetings be held on the last Tuesday of the month from 9.30 am – 12.30 pm;

THAT Council note the Mayoral Minute on Pentarch Oaklands being nominated as a finalist in the Land Forces 2022 Innovation Awards and wish the company good luck in the award announcement.

Queen Elizabeth II

On behalf of Federation Council, we offer our deepest sympathies to His Majesty King Charles III, The Royal Family, and all those across the world mourning the loss of Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II.

Queen Elizabeth II's reign was the longest of any British monarch serving for 70 years.

We will remember Queen Elizabeth II for her kindness, dignity and unwavering commitment to the Commonwealth and her people. She was a beloved Monarch, mother, grandmother and great grandmother.

May she rest in peace.

I would now please ask Councillors, Staff and public members within this chamber to join me in a minute silence in honour of Queen Elizabeth II. 

Cr David Fahey OAM
The Mayor acknowledged that Cr Fahey was awarded his Masters in Local Government.

346/2022FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and David Fahey
  1. THAT Council note the report on progress of the Federation Council Annual Financial Statements for the year ended 30 June 2022; and
  2. THAT Council authorise the signing of the declaration as follows:-
The General Purpose Financial Report has been prepared in accordance with:
  • The Local Government Act 1993 (as amended) and the Regulations made thereunder,
  • The Australian Accounting Standards and professional pronouncements, and
  • The Local Government Code of Accounting Practice and Financial Reporting.
To the best of our knowledge and belief, this Report:
  • Presents fairly the Council’s operating result and financial position for the year, and
  • Accords with Council’s accounting and other records.
The Special Purpose Financial Reports have been prepared in accordance with:
  • The NSW Government Policy Statement “Application of National Competition Policy to Local Government”.
  • The Office of Local Government Guidelines “Pricing & Costing for Council Businesses - A Guide to Competitive Neutrality”.
  • The Local Government Code of Accounting Practice and Financial Reporting.
  • The Department of Water and Energy Best-Practice Management of Water and Sewerage Guidelines.
To the best of our knowledge and belief, these Reports:
  • Present fairly the Operating Result and Financial Position for each of Council's declared business Activities for the year, and
  • Accord with Council’s accounting and other records.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr Sally Hughes reported on her attendance at the MDA Annual Conference 19-21 September 2022 and read out the following report:
 
MDA annual conference notes
Tour Monday 19th September, 2022
Participants were taken on a bus tour encompassing Dartmouth Dam and Hume Dam with lunch at the Mitta Pub. Dartmouth was hovering at around 99% capacity for four weeks – it consequently spilled on Wednesday 21st October, 2022 for the first time since 1996.
 
Dartmouth Dam has the largest capacity of any dam in the Murray–Darling Basin (3,856GL)
Jointly managed by the MDBA and Goulburn-Murray Water, Dartmouth Dam is the most upstream storage in the River Murray System and collects almost 10% of the system's inflow. The Mitta Mitta River flows from Dartmouth Dam into the Hume storage, which was at almost 97% capacity at this date.
 
Conference Wednesday 21st 
Speakers
Andrew McConville - Chief Executive of the Murray Darling Basin Authority.
Mr McConville outlined that ‘In addition to running the River Murray on behalf of Basin states, the MDBA hold state governments accountable to their commitments to the Basin Plan future and all that it delivers for the 2.3 million people who depend upon it for the livelihoods and for the communities.’
 
He stated the importance of balancing the needs of the environment and the rivers with the needs of irrigation communities, First Nations people, the tourism sector and the 2.2 million people who call the Basin home.
 
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese made a pre-election commitment to deliver 450 gigalitres of water to the environment — a target set out in the 2012 Murray-Darling Basin Plan. 
Mr McConville stated the environment is benefiting from the first decade of the Murray-Darling Basin Plan – the environmental water has been used in times of drought to benefit the environment and revitalise drought affected communities.
 
Unfortunately, the eighth MDBA report card shows seven state-managed water-saving projects are at high risk of not being delivered.
 
The Water Resource Plans set out detailed rules about who has rights to water, the licensing regime, when water can be extracted by agriculture, measures to protect water for the environment and rights to cultural water for indigenous people.
 
All other states have now had their plans accredited but NSW, which had the largest number of plans to produce, has been lagging.
 
Troy Grant- Inspector General of water compliance
The Inspector General of water compliance stated that “Water is integral to everything”. He spoke about the very real science provided by CSIRO that indicates we face a 30% decline in water availability, more extreme weather events and rising temperatures.
 
Mr Grant committed to looking into community concerns about how the Murray Darling Basin Authority (MDBA) was managing the river and how the Commonwealth Environmental Water Holder (CEWH)   was using its environmental water. The evidence-based investigation has shown, contrary to common belief that the agencies are performing their functions according to their obligations.
 
He spoke about new gauging stations were introduced in 2020 to increase transparency in water usage. Advances in technology, in particular- Telemetry provide a very accurate reading. Mr Grant stated that there are opportunities and scope for improvement.
 
Tanya Plibersek – Federal Water Minister 
Tanya Plibersek gave an address at the conference and confirmed that ‘no options are off the table’ to secure the basin’s future. The Victorian and New South Wales governments, and the federal Coalition oppose buying water entitlements from farmers, arguing enough water has been bought back from irrigators as part of the Murray-Darling Basin Plan.
 
Rod Knight - CEO Water Stewardship Asia Pacific
Mr Knight explained that Water Stewardship a holistic approach to water management. Water stewardship can be used as a tool in balancing the needs of the environment and communities.
 
Securing the health of the Basin will require a range of approaches to balance social, economic, environmental and cultural needs, and Water Stewardship has an important role to play. It seeks to bring businesses and communities together in a locally-driven, multi-stakeholder collaboration on shared water challenges, in a way that drives change at the catchment scale and can be independently assessed against the international Water Stewardship Standard.
 
Investment in the capacity to upskill people and transform business cultures, requiring a shift in focus from water efficiency to a holistic approach where the contribution to catchment outcomes is recognised and valued.
 
Extra information about the Role of Stewardship
Adoption of Good water management via stewardship requires a range of strategies
  • Social/cultural
  • Environmental sustainability
  • Economic benefit
 
Good water governance
  • Sustainable water balance- no long term effect on the environment
  • Good water quality
  • Good sanitation
 
Thinking Points: What if………

The steps guide organisations to:
  1. Understand your water use, risks, impacts, and opportunities at a site and local catchment-level.
  2. Develop and commit to a water stewardship plan, prioritising targets, with actions and responsibilities for improved water management and outcomes.
  3. Implement your plan and improve your water impacts.
  4. Evaluate your actions and revise your plan for continuous improvement.
  5. Communicate your water actions responsibly and transparently.
 
Water stewardship Asia Pacific
Rod Knight CEO

Congratulations to Jeff Duryea racing on the magnificent victory by Front Page in the prestigious 2022 Kosciusko horse race event at Randwick.
 
The Kosciuszko is the world’s richest race for country-trained horses, carrying $2 million in prizemoney.  The Kosciuszko race is a 1200 metre sprint contest run under set weights and penalties conditions on the same day as The TAB Everest at Royal Randwick on Saturday 15 October 2022.
 
Council will look to formally congratulate Duryea Racing and connections including the likelihood of some involvement at a fitting event that the Corowa Race Club will be sure to hold at a race meeting in the future.

The Mayor made special note of the work of Council’s Local Emergency Management Officers (LEMO’s), Director Engineering Steve Carmichael and Director Development and Environmental Services, Susan Appleyard (Deputy LEMO and Acting LEMO whilst Steve was on leave.  Their work and the entire Council staff over the last few months have been amazing and so much appreciated, including the weekly meetings, and the work out in the field.
 
On behalf of Council and all ratepayers, I thank them for the work they have done and will continue to do with the large amounts of water coming into our area.
 
The Mayor also advised Cr Fahey spoke at the recent Australian Local Government Roads Conference in Hobart, to support a motion to secure further much needed funding for Council’s road networks due to the flooding damage. 
 
Cr Longley asked that the outdoor staff receive a great big pat on the back for the amount of work they have put in, particularly around the Howlong area under extraordinary circumstances, and they are a credit to our Council.
 
365/2022FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and David Fahey
THAT Council note the Mayoral Minute.

400/2022FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Fahey and Gail Law
  1. THAT Council note Delegate Report from Councillor David Fahey OAM - National Local Roads and Transport Congress;
  2. THAT Council investigate using services from ARRB (NTRO) and enquire into innovative and cost saving measures for the road infrastructure that they may be able to deliver; and
  3. THAT Council pass a resolution to support LGNSW in lobbying State and Federal Members in NSW. That calls on the NSW and Federal Governments to take action on the Statewide Roads Emergency and help our regional and rural communities bounce back from the devastation caused by this year’s floods.
As part of the Statewide Roads Emergency, LGNSW is calling for:
  • An acceleration and significant increase in funding for the $1.1 billion Fixing Local Roads and Fixing Country Bridges program.
  • A boost to Road Block Grant funding to compensate for the damage to the regional road network.
  • New funding to provide councils with plant machinery and skilled workers to expedite road repairs.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"In the mayoral minute today, I would like to take the opportunity to formally knowledge two passing’s that have occurred since the last meeting of Council.
 
Julie Bartlett of Balldale passed away on Monday and on behalf of Council I would like to extend our thoughts to Julie’s family and friends.
 
Julie was a valued and upstanding community member of Balldale. She was an inspiration to the community and showed amazing Australian values such as loyalty, commitment, courage, support and dependability.
 
Julie was the Balldale Rural Fire Brigade secretary, Our Town Balldale Inc secretary, and Back to Balldale Ball president. Julie was awarded Balldale local achiever of the year at Federation Council‘s Australia Day awards ceremony on Thursday.
 
Julie was very proud of her achievements as are her family, community and Council today.
 
I would also like to acknowledge the passing of my son Brodie Pigdon recently. The last few weeks have been extremely difficult for myself and my family. I would like to take the opportunity to thank you all in this room and wider community for the support and love, with messages, phone calls, cards and donations to Boys to the Bush in honour of Brodie mean so much to my family and myself.
 
In honour of Julie and Brodie, I would like to ask Council to stand for one minute silence to pay their respects to their amazing lives.
  
4/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Gail Law and Andrew Kennedy
THAT Council note the Mayoral Minutes.

Amendment
Moved by Councillors Aaron Nicholls and Rowena Black 

Add the following points to the recommendation
  1. THAT Council receive and note the report on the Special Rate Variation application;
  2. THAT Council endorse the Special Rate Variation application to be submitted to IPART; 
  3. THAT Council request a report on additional pensioner concession options that could be applied to assist ratepayers most impacted by the proposed SRV increase.

  5. THAT Council request a report from the Manager Communication and Engagement specific to the planned community engagement strategy for
  1. the remainder of the SRV application and implementation process; and
  2. Council generally relative to the planned implementation of a new  overarching Communication Strategy planned for this year.

25/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and Shaun Whitechurch
The Federation Council (“the Council”) resolves:
  1. pursuant to s. 296(2) and (3) of the Local Government Act 1993 (NSW) (“the Act”) that an election arrangement be entered into by contract for the Electoral Commissioner to administer all elections of the Council.
  2. pursuant to s. 296(2) and (3) of the Act, as applied and modified by s. 18, that a council poll arrangement be entered into by contract for the Electoral Commissioner to administer all council polls of the Council.
  3. pursuant to s. 296(2) and (3) of the Act, as applied and modified by s. 18, that a constitutional referendum arrangement be entered into by contract for the Electoral Commissioner to administer all constitutional referenda of the Council.
Further the Council resolves to share 2024 electoral costs with Berrigan Shire and Murrumbidgee Councils where opportunities arise.

95/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and David Longley
THAT Council endorse the following applications for grant funds:
  1. $2,000 cash contribution for the Corowa High School P & C to support the cost of the Breakfast Club to supply other foods (e.g. Fresh fruit) to meet students' nutritional needs and support healthy food and lifestyle choices.
  2. $3,000 cash contribution for the Mulwala Football Netball Club to replace the current outdated steel goal posts with aluminium, in-line with AFL minimum standards.
  3. $1,592 cash contribution for the Corowa Rescue Squad to purchase a computer to support volunteers undertaking mandatory on-line training.
  4. $2,050 cash contribution for the Mulwala Progress Association to purchase a defibrillator for Tunzafun to enable response to emergency cardiac situations.
  5. $2,000 cash contribution for the Howlong Golf Club Resort for a Family Fun Day, a free community event with an array of kids activities and music.
  6. $3,000 cash contribution for the Corowa Pony Club to construct an arena fence to support safe participation.
  7. $2,000 cash contribution for the Urana Campdraft Incorporated to support the 2024 Urana Campdraft, including youth events.
  8. $1,500 cash contribution for Intereach to support the delivery of a skate workshop at the Corowa Skate Park, providing free skills development and a fun day for young people.
  9. $1,250 cash contribution for the Corowa Public School P&C to host an Open Garden event, showcasing and celebrating the gardening and environmental success achieved by students and the volunteers and community groups who have shared their knowledge and support on the sustainable garden practices. 
  10. $1,000 cash contribution for the Mulwala Public School P & C to host the Mulwala Kite Festival, a free community event also aimed at attracting visitors.
  11. $2,000 cash contribution for the Corowa Agricultural Society to support the Corowa Agricultural Show, including educational activities.
  12. $3,000 cash contribution for the Corowa Historical Society to hold the 130th Anniversary of the 1893 Corowa Conference.
  13. $2,000 cash Contribution for the Oaklands and District Lions Club to hold the Santa in The Park event, a free community event for Christmas. 
  14. $1,700 cash contribution for the Corowa SHE Shed to purchase wood working equipment. 
  15. $2,500 cash contribution for the Daysdale Hall Committee to support the cost of the installation of updated visitor and historical signage and a walk through shed.

113/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Fahey and Shaun Whitechurch
  1. THAT Council writes to the Treasurer, the Minister for Emergency Services, the Minister for Local Government and local State Member(s):
    1. Expressing Council’s strong opposition to the NSW Government’s last minute decision to impose an enormous Emergency Services Levy (ESL) cost increase on councils for 2023/24 by scrapping the ESL subsidy for councils and at a time after Council has publicly advertised its 23/24 draft Operational Plan incorporating the draft 23/24 budget to the community;
    2. Noting that as a consequence of the late notice of the 73% increase in the State Emergency Service budget and an 18% increase in the Fire and Rescue NSW budget, Council’s ordinary rate increase of 4.3% (should the special rate variation not be approved, and should Council therefore apply the maximum allowable rate peg), has been significantly eroded to the amount of $174,000.
    3. Calling on the NSW Government to take immediate action to:
      1. restore the ESL subsidy in 2023/24
      2. urgently introduce legislation to decouple the ESL from the rate peg to enable councils to recover the full cost
      3. develop a fairer, more transparent and financially sustainable method of funding critically important emergency services in consultation with local government.
  2. THAT Council writes to the Chair of the Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal (IPART) advising that Council’s forced emergency services contribution is manifestly disproportionate to the 2023/24 rate cap, which will result in additional financial stress should Council not receive its special rate variation application; and
  3. THAT Council writes to the President of LGNSW seeking the Association’s ongoing advocacy to bring about a relief in the burden of Councils’ emergency services contribution.

138/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Fahey and Shaun Whitechurch
  1. THAT Federation Council engage a consultant to undertake an independent peer reviewed business case study on the financial sustainability of Federation Council and the advantages/disadvantages of amalgamation;
  2. THAT Council allocate adequate funding to cover the cost of the review, being approximately $130,000, in this year’s budget from savings, and receive a further report at the June ordinary meeting; and
  3. THAT Council consider engaging the preeminent Professor Joseph Drew and his independent nominees, Professor Masato Miyazaki from Saitama University, Japan and Professor Diogo Ferreira from IST Portugal to undertake the peer reviewed study, considering Professor Drew is a Local Government specialist and is also very experienced in the issues and costs associated with amalgamated Councils.

THAT Council note the confidential report forwarded under separate cover, presenting the submissions received, and the assessment by Councils External Advisor, and the assessment of this process to date, to allow consideration of the engagement of a firm to undertake an independent peer reviewed business case study on the financial sustainability of Federation Council and the advantages and disadvantages of amalgamation.
  3. THAT Council defer the remainder of the report until a closed session of the Council meeting under Section 10A (2) of the Local Government Act and Clause 14.1 of Council’s Code of Meeting Practice to further discuss this item and pass any further resolutions, as the attachment to this report contains matters and information are the following:  (c) information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business
    (d) commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed
       (i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it.
  4. THAT in the closed session, that Council pass a further resolution/s to appoint a firm to deliver the Independent peer reviewed business case study on the financial sustainability of Federation Council and the advantages and disadvantages of amalgamation, should they wish to appoint one of the firms who have submitted a quotation, after being invited following the Request for Quote process.

173/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and Gail Law
  1. THAT Council note the report on the issues raised in the report by the Rural Fire Services (RFS) volunteers across the Federation Berrigan Zone/Council areas;
  2. THAT Council meet with the Councils of Albury, Greater Hume and Berrigan, to formally discuss these issues; where relevant to each of those Councils;
  3. THAT Council meet with RFS local (Southern Border), Area Command and State Wide management/commissioner level, to further discuss and seek resolutions to the issues raised in particular those covered by motions 4) a) e) and f) below, unanimously passed at the meeting at Rennie;
  4. THAT Council supports in principle the following motions as passed at the RFS Brigade Group Captains meeting held at Rennie on 21 June 2023 being -
    1. Motion- That the Bush Fire Management committee, not be merged with Greater Hume and is kept within the Local Government areas of Federation and Berrigan.  (strategic matter - involves Council)
    2. Motion - To retrofit where applicable to Cat 1s upgrades with monitors. (operational matter to be dealt with between RFS and members).
    3. Motion - That future bids and replacement tankers for Rural Brigades be Cat1 Single Cabs or Cat 6s. (operational matter to be dealt with between RFS and members). 
    4. Motion - Training day time and place to be decided by the group. (operational matter to be dealt with between RFS and members).
    5. Motion – Expression from Howlong Brigade to move to Group 3 (Hume Shire) NOT endorsed by Group 2 brigades and Fed zone.(strategic matter - involves Council). 
    6. Motion - To reopen the Corowa RFS office on a full-time basis and to immediately have the Federation Zone, incorporating the local government areas of Federation and Berrigan councils operating as a “Stand alone zone” with its full staffing entitlements again, hence ceasing the voluntary teaming arrangement with Greater Hume Zone in line with the agreed ability to review this arrangement.  (strategic matter - involves Council and would need support of Neighbouring Council Berrigan, and RFS, and consultation with Albury and Greater Hume Councils). 
  5. THAT Council works with the Rural Fire Service and the Councils of Albury, Greater Hume and Berrigan, to develop a new Rural Fire District Service Level Agreement as a matter of urgency, and receives further reports on this matter and the other matters as raised above, especially in relation to motions labelled a) e) and f), as they progress, with the other motions being more operational matters for the RFS to determine with their brigades and Council staff if appropriate.

176A/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Shaun Whitechurch and Andrew Kennedy
THAT Council note the report on the finalisation of the Terms of Reference for the Independent peer reviewed Business Case Study on Federation Council, being undertaken by the Institute for Regional Futures (University of Newcastle) and that Council advise the public of the final Terms of Reference at this meeting by a further resolution made during this report.

176B/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Gail Law and Shaun Whitechurch
THAT Council adopt the terms of reference (TOR) for this Independent Peer Reviewed Business Case Study are as follows:
  1. A review and provide commentary of the validity of the former Corowa Shire Council’s merger proposal submitted to the NSW State Government including all potential efficiencies and savings outlined in that report i.e. $41M over 20 years.
  2. Review NSW Minister’s proposal (the KPMG report) on the Corowa and Urana merger proposal including (but not limited to) a review and commentary on whether the efficiencies and savings outlined in that study and were achieved, and if not why?
  3. A comparison of Council’s financial performance since merger as opposed to the combined financial performance of the Corowa and Urana Councils prior to merger.
  4. Analysis and provide commentary on the projected financial sustainability of the Federation Council from 2023 onwards including (but not limited to); 
    (a) The circumstances leading to the current financial position of Council and
    (b) an investigation of various options for improving the financial sustainability – Prepare a gap analysis on options that will include additional sources of revenue and changes to expenditure profiles.
  5. Whether, in accordance with section 263 (3) (e5) of the NSW Local Government Act, 1993 (the Act) there is a need (or desirability) to divide the Council area into Wards to ensure effective representation.
  6. Any other matters of section 263 (3) of the Act considered relevant.
  7. Investigate options for engaging with NSW State Government to try to mitigate any issues identified. 
  8. After completing TOR 1 to 7 investigate the need, timing and conduct of a potential special rate variation application.

206/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Fahey and Aaron Nicholls
  1. THAT Council note the report on possible motions for the 2023 LGNSW Annual Conference;
  2. THAT the Mayor, 2 x Councillors (to be nominated) and the General Manager be delegated to attend the LGNSW Annual Conference from 12-14 November;
  3. THAT the Mayor and 1 Councillor (to be nominated) be Council’s nominated voting delegates; and
  4. THAT Council consider and endorse the below motions to the 2023 LGNSW Annual Conference.
    • THAT Local Government NSW lobbies the State and Federal Governments for improvement in Mobile Phone coverage and a more strategic approach to developing infrastructure across the country.
    • THAT Local Government NSW lobby the State Government for improvements to air space management rules in NSW Dams such as Lake Hume to lessen impacts of downstream flooding.
    • THAT Local Government NSW lobbies the State and Federal Government for a more aligned approach to their grant funding schemes to allow Councils to better take advantage of required funding.
    • THAT Local Government NSW lobby the State Government for improved funding for critical water and sewer infrastructure upgrades and renewal projects.
    • THAT Local Government NSW lobby the State Government for financial support for planners and building surveyors at a local government level throughout NSW.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr Patrick Bourke announced that the first order of business is the election of mayor and vacates the chair for the returning officer (General Manager) who will conduct the election. 

231/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Shaun Whitechurch and Gail Law
  1. THAT Council elect a Deputy Mayor as well as the Mayor;
  2. THAT Council determine that the method of election for the Office of Mayor and Deputy Mayor is by way of ordinary ballot (secret ballot); and
  3. THAT the election be conducted by the returning officer and the results communicated.

The returning officer advised the meeting of the method of voting. 
 
Election of Mayor 
The returning officer read out the name of the nominee and confirmation that the nominee has accepted the nomination.
 
As there was only one nominee for the role of mayor, the returning officer declared that Councillor Pat Bourke is elected as mayor until the September 2024 LG election.
  
Election of Deputy Mayor 
The returning officer read out the names of the nominees and seeks confirmation that the nominee has accepted the nomination.
  
Two nominations were received for the role of Deputy Mayor being Councillor Rowena Black and Councillor Shaun Whitechurch.
  
The returning officer announced the names of the candidates for deputy mayor being Councillor Rowena Black and Councillor Shaun Whitechurch and wrote each name on a slip of paper and deposits it in a box.  The first name out of the box will be written first on the tally sheet, with second name out being written second on the tally sheet.
 
Director Shannon drew the Deputy Mayor voting candidate out of the box to determine the order to be written on the voting cards, with Cr Whitechurch being drawn out, then being listed first on the ballot paper.
 
Councillors will appear on ballet paper in the following order:
Councillor Shaun Whitechurch
Councillor Rowena Black
 
 Tally
 Councillor Whitechurch 5 votes
 Councillor Black 3 votes
 
 The returning officer, Adrian Butler declared that Councillor Shaun Whitechurch has the higher number of votes and declared that Councillor Whitechurch is elected as Deputy Mayor until the September 2024 LG election.
  
 Mayor resumes the chair - Councillor Patrick Bourke occupied the chair.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"In my mayoral minute today, I would like to take this opportunity to formally acknowledge five passings that have recently occurred in our community. I would firstly like to acknowledge Maryann Herbert, Margaret Flynn and Marjorie Saines.
 
All three ladies were much loved stalwarts in our community and will be dearly missed. Maryann was an integral member of our Corowa Aquatic Centre Pool Advisory Committee, and a huge advocate for creating the amazing centre that sits next to us today. She also supported many young people over the years with her passionate involvement in Girl Guides and will be dearly missed.
 
Margaret Flynn worked for Council in our tourism department for over ten years. Margie was not only a paid employee but she also volunteered her time on many occasions to support tourism events and activities over the years.
 
Marj Saines and her husband Frank volunteered for Council for over 15 years not only at the Visitor Information Centre but also at many Tourism and Council events.
 
Marj organised the annual art show held in Corowa for many years and contributed to this sector in many ways over an extended period of time.
 
I would also like to formally extend my deepest sympathies to the family and friends of Daniel Mofitt and Kasie Parker who tragically lost their lives in a motor vehicle accident that has devastated our community. My ongoing thoughts remain with everyone affected by this tragic incident. Please continue to support one another.  
 
In honour of these community members I would now like to ask the gallery to stand for a minutes silence to pay our respects.

273/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Sally Hughes and Andrew Kennedy
THAT Council endorse the following applications for grant funds:
  1. $1,000 cash contribution to the Morundah Bush Entertainment Committee to assist with the cost of hosting the Peter Denehey Concert at Morundah.
  2. 7 cash contribution to the Sing Australia - Corowa to support the cost of purchasing new music books.
  3. $2,500 cash contribution to the Mulwala Progress Association to support the cost of purchasing lighting & decorations for the Mulwala Christmas tree.
  4. $1,750 cash contribution to the Savernake School of the Arts Reserve Trust to assist with the cost of hosting the Festival of Small Halls at Savernake.
  5. $3,000 cash contribution to the Annual Riverina Harvest Ball Committee Inc. to assist with the cost of cement and stencil works at the Oaklands Memorial Hall.
  6. $1,000 cash contribution to the Khaki Vehicle Enthusiasts Inc. towards the cost of event hats, plaques, and participant packs at the 44th Corowa Swim-in and Military Vehicle Gathering.
  7. $758 cash contribution to the Corowa & District Historical Society towards the cost of getting an upgrade to their computer memory and backup storage.
  8. $1,000 cash contribution to Intereach Inc- Corowa towards the cost of hosting “Mocktails and Masterpieces” an arts initiative as part of International Day of People with Disability. 
  9. $2,500 cash contribution to Mulwala Community Garden Inc. towards the cost of the Mulwala Community Garden signage and advertising.
  10. $3,000 cash contribution to the Mulwala Football Netball Club to support the cost of hosting the NETFIT Coaching Masterclass – Train like an elite netballer in Mulwala.
  11. $2,415 cash contribution to the Corowa Business Chamber to further scope and seek community consultation on their proposed Volunteer Training Program.
  12. $1,750 to the Howlong Golf Club in partnership with Amaranth Foundation to assist with the cost of hosting an all-abilities golf workshop in Howlong.
  13. $2,500 to the Our Town Balldale Committee to assist with the cost of hosting the Balldale Annual Summer Events Program.
  14. $1,750 to the Oaklands CWA to assist with the cost of hosting the CWA of NSW Women’s Dinner in Oaklands.
  15. $1,750 to The Inner Wheel of Corowa District to assist with the cost of hosting an International Women’s Day Lunch in Corowa.

New Motion
277/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Shaun Whitechurch and David Fahey
  1. THAT Council select Model 3 Tiered supervision as the preferred service delivery model at Corowa Aquatic Centre;
  2. THAT Council after fully implemented revisit the financial performance of the aquatic centre after 12 months of operation under this model;
  3. THAT Council request that council staff undertake engagement with affected staff as per the requirements under the NSW Local Government Award and consider feedback from staff about this workplace change prior to making a final decision to adopt Model 3; and
  4. THAT Council request council staff to further investigate service deliver model options for Howlong Swimming Pool and provide further information to Council for consideration.

The Mayor would like to request that a minutes silence be held in memory of Zoe Wilson of Corowa. Zoe was aged 25 years when she passed away on the 15 September. Zoe's family have shared with Council that she was a beautiful and much loved member not only of their family unit, but for many people in the community who knew Zoe.  Zoe unfortunately suffered from Anorexia, a severe mental illness for nearly a decade and the suffering from this became too much so that she unfortunately took her own life.  Zoe's family have highlighted that our community needs more awareness of Anorexia, and the mental illness impacts associated with this. On behalf of Council, our ongoing thoughts and condolences are extended to the Wilson family and we commend them for sharing their unimaginable loss to increase awareness and encourage members of the community who are struggling with conditions such as this to seek support and guidance.

300/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Fahey and Shaun Whitechurch
  1. THAT Council note the report on Council’s tourism services;
  2. THAT Council reduce the 
    1. service level for tourism services to:
      1. Provide a manned visitor information service 5 days or 29 hours per week in the Council administration building, with visitor information available through electronic means outside of manned hours.
      2. Provide financial support to Yarrawonga Mulwala Tourism to undertake visitor information services from Yarrawonga
      3. Deliver 4 x seasonal tourism campaigns and 2 x regional collaborative campaigns (incorporating the remaining campaigns for 2023/24 into the SRV funded ($60,000) North Of The Murray (NOTM) Destination Marketing Strategy campaigns
      4. Deliver 1 x $10,000 campaign with the Corowa Tourism Advisory Committee
      5. Maintain North of the Murray section of regional website (incl. access to ATDW and state and federal links)
      6. Provide town maps and brochures (for VIC and accommodation providers)
      7. Maintain membership of Murray Regional Tourism
    2. operating budget for tourism services by $132,000 in the 2023/24 budget and the associated future year forecasts for the amended level of service in the Long Term Financial Plan
  3. THAT Council increase the operating budget for planning services by $110,000 in the 2023/24 budget and Long Term Financial Plan future year forecasts;
  4. THAT Council reserve $15,000 in the 2023/24 budget for the Plan of Management for the Urana Caravan Park and repairs to the swimming pool manager’s residence, if cost effective; and 
  5. THAT Council establish an operating budget of $7,000 for Community Events Fee Rebate Fund and authorise the General Manager to authorise reimbursement of s68 application fees when the event is a community event and is conducted by an applicant that is not operating for private gain.

295/2023FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Aaron Nicholls and David Fahey
  1. THAT Council receive and note the minutes of the Urana Progress Association Committee General Meeting dated 3 October 2023 (23/49019);
  2. THAT Council receive and note the minutes of the Urana Progress Association Committee AGM dated 3 October 2023 (23/49018);
  3. THAT Council note the matters raised of the Urana Progress Association Committee minutes dated 3 October 2023; 
  4. THAT Council endorse the office bearers:
    • President: Barry Paterson 
    • Vice President: Wanda Oram-Miles 
    • Secretary/Treasurer: Wendy Mallon 
  5. THAT Council note the following and respond to the Urana Progress Association Committee via letter with the following:
    1. Note that the Federation Council has prioritised Macknight Park toilets for redevelopment in 2024 subject to funding, and that the Committee is encouraged to assist Council in seeking funding for the Courthouse toilets to be upgraded to meet modern standards/requirements, and note that the possibility of a cemetery toilet is a new build and Council is prioritising renewal and upgrades of existing facilities over new buildings,
    2. Note that the Bird Aviary grant has been submitted and that Council does not have funds for any contribution and the Progress Association will need to meet any ongoing costs associated with a water feature installation.
    3. Advise Council is not endorsing any Electric Vehicle installations on Council/Public Land/Crown Land managed by Council due to the ongoing costs associated with running the chargers and maintenance/repairs eg from vandalism and encourages private businesses to take up this offer, and should a private business wish to use Council land, this could be considered under an agreement.
    4. Note the request for additional signage and refer this matter to relevant staff to discuss with the Committee.

  1. THAT Council note the report on progress of the Federation Council Annual Financial Statements for the year ended 30 June 2023; and
  2. THAT Council authorise the signing of the declaration as follows:-
The General Purpose Financial Report has been prepared in accordance with:
  • The Local Government Act 1993 (as amended) and the Regulations made thereunder,
  • The Australian Accounting Standards and professional pronouncements, and
  • The Local Government Code of Accounting Practice and Financial Reporting.
To the best of our knowledge and belief, this Report:
  • Presents fairly the Council’s operating result and financial position for the year, and
  • Accords with Council’s accounting and other records.
The Special Purpose Financial Reports have been prepared in accordance with:
  • The NSW Government Policy Statement “Application of National Competition Policy to Local Government”.
  • The Office of Local Government Guidelines “Pricing & Costing for Council Businesses - A Guide to Competitive Neutrality”.
  • The Local Government Code of Accounting Practice and Financial Reporting.
  • The Department of Water and Energy Best-Practice Management of Water and Sewerage Guidelines.
To the best of our knowledge and belief, these Reports:
  • Present fairly the Operating Result and Financial Position for each of Council's declared business Activities for the year, and
  • Accord with Council’s accounting and other records.

35/2024FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Longley and Gail Law
  1. THAT Council note the available NSW Severe Weather and Flood Grant of $1.0 million and the likely insurance funds available through Statewide Mutual of $2.0 million;
  2. THAT Council note that expenditure totalling $1,012,000 has already been expended or committed as a result of the immediate and ongoing response to the flood;
  3. THAT Council approve the following actions, remediation and/or repairs as part of Council's response to the 2022 flood event:
    1. Corowa Civic Centre
      1. Abandon basement facilities
      2. Provide alternative amenities which will support future flood proofing of the building and meet staff welfare needs
    2. Corowa Civic Bowls
      1. Provide alternative amenities, subject to further stakeholder engagement
      2. Minor repairs umpires' box, subject to further stakeholder engagement
    3. Corowa Rutherglen Football Netball Club
      1. Continue to provide temporary facilities in the short to medium term
      2. Progress design for a future new building with stakeholder input
      3. Demolish flood damaged clubhouse
    4. Ball Park Caravan Park, Corowa
      1. Repair or replace the camp kitchen (first stage)
      2. Demolish the cystic fibrosis units (first stage)
      3. Address full remediation when Ball Park Masterplan is progressed (second stage)
    5. Memorial Park Toilet Block, Howlong
      1. Provide a new demountable toilet block and install septic tank with pump out system
    6. Lions Park Toilet Block
      1. Replace failed effluent disposal trenches with a septic tank with pump out system
    7. Other smaller assets:
      1. Repair any damage sustained to the fishing platform at Rowers Park, Corowa once damage assessment report is received
      2. Repair the damage sustained to the retaining wall at Memorial Park, Howlong as per structural engineer assessment
      3. Repair the damaged sustained to the retaining wall at Corowa Lagoon as per structural engineer assessment
  4. THAT Council endorse the allocation of the funding from NSW Severe Weather & Flood Grant (Category D) as follows:
    1. Temporary staff wages (12 months) and consultancy fees for project administration and management $150,000
    2. Emergency Management Council Capacity Building and Community Resilience, including wages for a temporary staff member for 12 months $150,000
    3. Design and/or repair or remediation of flood damaged community assets $700,000 split across the following assets:
      1. Corowa Civic Centre ($75,000)
      2. Corowa Civic Bowls Club ($125,000)
      3. Rowers Park, Corowa ($175,000)
      4. Howlong public toilets (Lions Park and Memorial Park Howlong ($225,000)
  5. THAT Council endorse the allocation of the remaining funds, subject to receipt of funds following approval of insurance claim, as follows:
    1. Corowa Civic Centre - provide alternative amenities ($488,000)
    2. Ball Park Caravan Park - repair camp kitchen, purchase new industrial dryer and repair rear gate post ($100,000)
    3. Corowa Rutherglen Football Netball Club - contribution to continued temporary accommodation and contribution to a new building ($400,000)
  6. THAT the 2023/2024 budget be adjusted to reflect the additional income and expenditure from the grant and claim, less any previous budget adjustments processed.

22A/2024FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Shaun Whitechurch and David Longley
  1. THAT Council receive and note the findings of the LGNSW Cost Shifting report for the 2021/2022 financial year;
  2. THAT a copy of the cost shifting report be placed on Council’s website so that our communities can access it; and

Murray Water Levels – Mayor spoke with NSW Minister for Water Rose Jackson.
Globe Hotel – Mayor advised he and the Deputy Mayor visited the Globe Hotel, Sanger Street, Corowa, to discuss the redevelopment proposal.
Free Press – Mayor noted departure of Journalist Adrienne Hartnett and welcome the new Journalist Kellie Shepherd.

  1. THAT Council note the report on the 2024 Murray Darling Association (MDA) 80th National Conference and AGM;
  2. THAT Council nominate Councillor Sally Hughes to attend the conference; and
  3. THAT Council lodge the following motions for the region 1 MDA meeting, to then if carried, be referred to the MDA meeting - 
    • Requesting more consideration by the Murray Darling Basin Authority, of maintaining higher Murray river levels during peak tourism times, to avoid the instance this January in Corowa especially, where the low river level proved a danger to those using the river, and resulted in lots of visitors leaving early due to not being able to Ski on the Murray in Corowa, and some not coming at all.
    • Encouraging cultural water to be used into areas such as the Urana Aquatic Centre/creek system.

76/2024FC   RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Gail Law
  1. THAT Council note the report on the Planning and Development resources;
  2. THAT an independent consultant be appointed to complete the service review for the Planning and Development Services;
  3. THAT pending sufficient budget being available in this year, additional short term administrative resources are added to assist in customer response times to development applications and construction certificate queries especially;
  4. THAT a further report be presented to the April Council meeting on progress; and
  5. THAT Council adopt recommendation 36 from the Independent review, being - Certain positions need to be funded and approved for the Planning and Development Team as soon as possible. Fixed-term positions need to be created for a plumbing inspector and an additional administration assistant until the back log becomes more manageable. New trainee positions may need to be funded and filled. It may be appropriate to fund the plumbing inspector and potentially other positions from the water and sewer fund. This matter has been allowed to go unresolved for too long and it is now evident that the stress of the situation is feeding on itself and having serious implications for the health and welfare of staff. 82/2024FC   RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Fahey and Gail Law
  1. THAT Council note the correspondence item 14.1.1 from the Yarrawonga Mulwala Bridge Centenary Committee seeking a donation towards a plaque to commemorate the bridge turning 100 this year; and
  2. THAT Council whilst appreciating the Yarrawonga Mulwala Bridge Centenary Committees interest in the current bridge and in holding an event to celebrate 100 years, not support the funding request for the following reasons –
    1. Council does not have a general donations budget, 
    2. Council does not own the bridge (it is owned by Transport for NSW – who could be approached if not already to part or wholly fund the plaque),
    3. By supporting a plaque, this could infer that Council has possible sentimental links to the current bridge, given on construction of a new bridge, the current position of Transport for NSW is that the current bridge will be demolished, and 
    4. Council will not take on ownership or any form of involvement in supporting keeping the current bridge for financial sustainability reasons, and the fact when the new bridge is built, the removal of the current bridge would allow greater access by boats into the area between the current bridge and the approved alignment of the new bridge.
(Carried)

Live Streaming of Council Meetings

All care will be taken to maintain the privacy of those in attendance, however as a visitor in the public gallery, your presence may be recorded. Statement of ethical obligations

108/2024FC   RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Rowena Black
  1. THAT Council note the updated report on the Planning and Development resources;
  2. THAT Council allocate additional resourcing of $630,346 per annum to the long term financial plan for positions and training for the planning and development services; and
  3. THAT Council endorse the submission of the Housing Support Program - Stream 1 application for the following:
    1. Finalisation of the Growth Management Strategy
      1. Consultant to co-ordinate and expedite the finalisation of the Growth Management Strategy for Federation Council Area.
      2. Undertake bushfire prone land assessment and mapping for the Federation Council area.
      3. Undertaken Biodiversity review and mapping for the Federation Council area.
    2. Cost Containment strategies for future dwelling applications
      1. Development of low pressure sewer servicing strategies for plains (flat) areas around the Council areas towns, notably Corowa and Mulwala.
      2. Development of onsite sewer management systems standards for across the Federation Council area, to define the land capability assessment limitation.
    3. Localised Resourcing
      1. Employment of a systems analyst to integrate all of the Council systems required for landuse planning and development since the introduction of the NSW Planning Portal.
      2. Establishment of an educational and concierge service for 12 months to assist the public in lodging development applications for housing.

132/2024FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and Aaron Nicholls
  1. THAT Council endorse the following motion to the Murray Darling Association (MDA) National Conference – 
    1. THAT Council urge the Murray Darling Basin Authority to give more consideration by the Murray Darling Basin Authority, of maintaining higher Murray river levels during peak tourism times, to avoid the instance this January in Corowa especially, where the low river level proved a danger to those using the river, and resulted in lots of visitors leaving early due to not being able to Ski on the Murray in Corowa, and some not coming at all.
  2. THAT Council engage further with the Narrandera and Wagga Wagga Local Aboriginal Land Councils and the Murray Darling Basin Authority in relation to seeking avenues to progress the option of using cultural water to be used into areas such as the Urana Aquatic Centre/creek system in dry times, and consider submitting a motion to the 2025 MDA National Conference if considered necessary.
  3. THAT Council further engage with the Commonwealth Environmental Water Holder for options within the Federation Council area. 

(Carried)

MOVED on the motion of Councillors David Fahey and Sally Hughes
  1. THAT Council note the report on the poll to be conducted in conjunction with the 2024 Local Government election for Federation Council;
  2. THAT Council endorse in principle the proposed community engagement strategy outlined; and
  3. THAT Council accept the estimate from the NSW Electoral Commission and carry forward $40,000 from unspent budgets in the Councillor Training and travel related costs budgets, and transfer to the 2024/24 Election budget to allow for the communication strategy costs and the additional costs charged by the NSW Electoral Commission to manage the poll.

An Amendment to the motion was moved by Councillor Shaun Whitechurch and seconded by Councillor David Fahey

Amending Motion

  1. THAT Council note the report on the poll to be conducted in conjunction with the 2024 Local Government election for Federation Council;

(Lost)

    3. Spiny burr and rabbits - Contact Council to request removal from Cemetery. Note from staff - add to customer request.
    4. 238/2024FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Gail Law and Aaron Nicholls
  1. THAT Council note the progress being made on the ten SRV recommendations from last year’s Independent Review by the University of Newcastle as attached;
  2. THAT Council note the following attachments  
    1. SRV 2025/26 - Community engagement statistics - University of Newcastle work (24/34616)
    2. Report on Pre-consultation Engagement with Stakeholder Groups 2024 (24/34933)
  3. THAT Council adopt the following reports as prepared by the University of Newcastle in August 2024:
    1. Financial Sustainability Report
    2. Capacity to Pay Report
    3. Efficiency Report
    4. Debt Capacity Report
    5. Community Engagement Report
  4. THAT Council defer consideration of two further recommendations from section 8, Measures to improve capacity to pay, being a) Coupon Booklets and b) Communication with respect to Landlords passing on the SRV to tenants, to the incoming Council;
  5. THAT Council endorse the progress of an application to the Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal for a 69.94% permanent Special Rate Variation over two years commencing 1 July 2025 and recommend such to the incoming Council; and
  6. THAT Council note and endorse the timelines associated with progressing an SRV application to IPART for implementation in 25/26.
(Carried)

The work done including the Independent Review undertaken in this time and it has seen the Council advance very well in his opinion. Congratulate all the staff as well for the hard work they have done and the path they have put the Council on, to go forward into the future. Wished Councillors have are retiring from Council all the best, and wished any Councils running for re-election the best also. The Mayor advised it has been a pleasure and an honour to be the Mayor for this term.
