","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[{"id":2386,"name":"Report","isUploaded":0,"reportTemplateId":1,"wordTemplateId":6,"pdfMediaFullPath":"stream/FEDERATION/tmp_a8f27dfcff.pdf","token":"300c4f67-c459-4229-b31a-3dd47b2ce53b","isPublic":true}],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[{"id":1046,"name":"5","eventId":241,"title":"Meetings/Engagements attended to by Mayor since the July 2024 Council Meeting","text":"Meetings/Engagements attended to by Mayor since the July 2024 Council Meeting","startTime":268,"duration":null,"itemId":4091,"sortOrder":6,"minutesSortOrder":6,"parentId":-1,"additionalParentId":-1}],"minutes":[]},{"id":4092,"name":"Verbal Reports from Delegates","parentId":3675,"sortOrder":44,"minutesSortOrder":44,"minutesParentId":3675,"outlineNumber":"1","fullOutlineNumber":"13.1.","htmlContent":"
  [OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL] [AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"
  • Councillor David Fahey thanked staff, Councillors and Mayor for their contributions across his term on Council. Wished those retiring to enjoy their time, and wished others all the very best also, and he thinks we have a great path forward and he hopes the new Council follow this track. He noted and thanked the Mayor for his advocacy.
  • Councillor Longley thanked the Council for his time on Council.

  • Cr Nicholls spoke about the many varied committees he was a delegate for and the amazing amount of work they get involved in, and thanked the staff, Councillors and the Mayor for their contributions and wished everyone well for the future, as he is not standing for re-election as he has relocated. Cr Nicholls commented on the need to continue the strong advocacy to ensure the Corowa Hospital does not further decline and he commented on the strengthened engagement with Aboriginal Culture including the Bangerang People. Cr Nicholls also commented on the appreciation he felt at being so respected as being as far as he knows, the only out gay person in a rural NSW Council.
  • Councillor Whitechurch thanked the Mayor, General Manager and Cr Law and wished everyone all the best also and those retiring, and those seeking re-election all the best and also thanked and praised the Senior Staff and all the way down through all staff.
  • Councillor Law reported on her attendance at the Ageing Well Committee meeting, and the strategy and praised the work of the committee and recommended the committee and hopes Councils supports it as far as it can. Cr Law also praised the work of the Youth Committee. Cr Law has also been involved with the Friends of the Library, Riverina Library and the Airport Committee. Cr Law gave thanks for her time on Council and thanked the Mayor and fellow Councillors and wished everyone all the best also.
 
Councillor Whitechurch left the meeting at 12.05 PM.
 
  • Councillor Sally Hughes reported on her attendance at the Historical Society AGM, Corowa Local Health Advisory Committee (LHAC) meeting and requested the Mayor and General Manager attend the Opening of the next MLHD LHAC forum to be held this time in Corowa, on the 5th and 6th of September. Councillor Hughes also thanked the Councillors around the table and it been an honour and privilege and thanked all the staff including the Executive staff.
  • Councillor Kennedy reported on his attendance at the Disability Inclusion Access Committee Plan (DIAP) meeting - visit to Mulwala, thanked Councillors and wished everyone all the best.
  • Councillor Rowena Black said it has been an enjoyable experience to be on Council and represent the people, and thanked Councillors also and all the staff, and wished everyone all the best.
 
Councillor Whitechurch returned to the meeting at 12.09 PM.

250/2024FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Fahey and Gail Law
THAT Council note the verbal reports from delegates.
(Carried)

234/2024FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Shaun Whitechurch and Gail Law
  1. THAT Council note the report on the attendance by the General Manager, at a meeting with local Member for Albury Mr Justin Clancy MP MLA and the Honourable Jihad Dib, Minister for Customer Service and Digital Government, Minister for Emergency Services, and Minister for Youth Justice;

254/2024FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Bott and Richard Nixon
  1. THAT Council note the report on the election of a Mayor and Deputy Mayor,  
  2. THAT Council resolve to also elect a Deputy Mayor, for a two year term in line with the Mayoral term,
  3. THAT the method of election for the Office of Mayor and Deputy Mayor be by way of open (show of hands) ballot,
  4. THAT the elections be conducted by the General Manager as the returning officer and results being votes for and against be read out and noted in the minutes.
(Carried)
​ 
Election of Mayor
Two nominations were received for the position of Mayor being Councillor Cheryl Cook and Councillor Derek Schoen.
 
Councillors were voted in the following order:
Councillor Derek Schoen               4 (Councillors Bott, Harrison, Nixon and Schoen)
Councillor Cheryl Cook                  5 (Councillors Black, Bourke, Cook, Kennedy and Wearne)
 
The returning officer, Adrian Butler declared that Councillor Cheryl Cook has the higher number of votes and declared that Councillor Cheryl Cook is elected Mayor for the ensuing two years.
 
Deputy Mayor
One nomination was received for the role of Deputy Mayor being Councillor Rowena Black. 
 
As there is only one nominee for the role of Deputy Mayor, the returning officer, Adrian Butler declared that Councillor Rowena Black is elected as Deputy Mayor for the ensuing two years.

Adjournment of Meeting
RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and David Harrison
THAT the meeting be adjourned for media opportunity at 09:46 AM.

Councillor Cook occupied the chair.

Resumption of Meeting
RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Rowena Black
THAT the meeting resumed at 10:12 AM with all Councillors present excluding Cr Bourke.

Councillor Patrick Bourke returned to the meeting at 10:13 AM.

Mayor Cook thanked everyone in the room for participating.   Mayor Cook offered commiserations to the other Mayoral nominee Councillor Schoen, and said he ran his best race and she looks forward to his energy and learning more on the ideas that he has and stated he has a lot to bring to the table. Mayor Cook is looking forward to working as a very collaborative team and would love to see a very positive feeling in the Chamber because the outcome of doing it any differently doesn’t always have a good outcome. Mayor Cook wants everyone to all work together and work strongly and move forward. Mayor Cook said we have some changes to make and that has been made very clear by the community, and also to take point of the wonderful hard decisions that were already made by the previous council.
 
Mayor Cook thanked Councillor Bourke for his 8 years of fantastic service as previous Mayor and said she knows how hard it is and they have watched the Mayor and Councillors Black and Kennedy, as the incumbents, and acknowledged that it has been a tough four years for the staff, the General manager, and Directors you didn’t work under a normal race the last four years and said she thinks everyone is aware of that.
 
To be tossed with the covid pandemic that sent everyone home, staff had to work from their homes and had to adjust to a new normal. Staff were then hit with the worst floods ever in 2022 that wiped out all of Ball Park Corowa, Urana, and the roads and it was a tough year and I just wanted to say congratulations and thank you for everything that you’ve done these past four years and I trust that we can take some of that on board here and we move forward with some of the new things that need to be done.

Pursuant to section 291A(1) (b) of the Local Government Act 1993 (the Act) Federation Council declares that casual vacancies occurring in the office of a councillor within 18 months after the last ordinary election of councillors for the Council on 14 September 2024 are to be filled by a countback of votes cast at that election for the office in accordance with section 291A of the Act and directs the general manager to notify the NSW Electoral Commissioner of the Council’s decision within 7 days of the decision.

256/2024FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Rowena Black
  1. THAT Council note the report on Local Government NSW 2024 Annual Conference - Nominate Councillor Delegate and Motions for Submission;
  2. THAT Council nominate Councillor Rowena Black to attend to the LGNSW Annual Conference from 17-19 November; and 
  3. THAT Council endorse the following motions for submission to the 2024  Local Government NSW Annual Conference:
    1. THAT Local Government NSW calls on the NSW Government to continue to review the planning portal to ensure improvements can be made to ease the burdens on Councils and Developers;
    2. THAT Local Government NSW calls on the NSW Government to increase funding for Telecommunications Infrastructure, specifically mobile phone coverage in regional and rural areas, and partner strategically with Councils, the Federal Government and Telco Providers to ensure a more co-ordinated strategic rollout of improvements to connectivity;
    3. THAT Local Government NSW calls on the NSW Government to reinstate the Stronger Country Communities Funding Grant program;
    4. THAT Local Government NSW calls on the NSW Government to increase funding for all Council's; and
    5. THAT Local Government NSW calls on the NSW Government to increase funding for Health Infrastructure, based a strategic needs based assessments.
(Carried)

During Committee of a Whole, Council agreed on the Councillor Delegates to the Reference/Advisory Groups/Organisations and Committees 
  
Also the following election below occurred during the Committee of a Whole, to determine the Riverina Water County Council delegate as required under the NSW Local Government Act 1993.

Election of Member to Riverina Water County Council Board
Two nominations were received for the board position with Riverina Water County Council being Councillor Patrick Bourke and Councillor David Bott.

Councillors were voted in the following order:
Councillor David Bott               2 (Councillors Bott and Schoen)
Councillor Patrick Bourke        5 (Councillors Black, Bourke, Cook, Harrison and Nixon)

The returning officer, Adrian Butler declared that Councillor Patrick Bourke has the higher number of votes and declared that Councillor Patrick Bourke is elected to the Board for Riverina Water County Council for the ensuing four years.

271/2024FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and Rowena Black
  1. THAT Council note the report on progress of the Federation Council Annual Financial Statements for the year ended 30 June 2024; and
  2. THAT Council authorise the signing of the declaration, subject to Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee recommendation, as follows:-
The General Purpose Financial Report has been prepared in accordance with:
  • The Local Government Act 1993 (as amended) and the Regulations made thereunder,
  • The Australian Accounting Standards and professional pronouncements, and
  • The Local Government Code of Accounting Practice and Financial Reporting.
To the best of our knowledge and belief, this Report:
  • Presents fairly the Council’s operating result and financial position for the year, and
  • Accords with Council’s accounting and other records.
The Special Purpose Financial Reports have been prepared in accordance with:
  • The NSW Government Policy Statement “Application of National Competition Policy to Local Government”.
  • The Office of Local Government Guidelines “Pricing & Costing for Council Businesses - A Guide to Competitive Neutrality”.
  • The Local Government Code of Accounting Practice and Financial Reporting.
  • The Department of Water and Energy Best-Practice Management of Water and Sewerage Guidelines.
To the best of our knowledge and belief, these Reports:
  • Present fairly the Operating Result and Financial Position for each of Council's declared business Activities for the year, and
  • Accord with Council’s accounting and other records.
(Carried)

Foreshadowed Motion
MOVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and David Bott
THAT Council 
  1. Note the resolution from the outgoing Council recommending progress of an application to the Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal for a 69.94% permanent Special Rate Variation over two years commencing 1 July 2025;
  2. Endorse the progress of work required for an application to the Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal to make the temporary Special Rate Variation permanent being 45.91%;
  3. That no future special rate variation be progressed or applied for until the workplace culture and productivity reforms are achieved and asset rationalisation and disposal are identified as per appendix 1a below;
  4. Progress on the updated 10 year Long Term Financial Plan to be placed on Council's website and public exhibition seeking community feedback for a period of 28 days;
  5. Update the recommended changes to the Delivery Program 2022-2026 (numbered 1 to 9) as outlined in this report, and for the updated Delivery Program 2022-2026 to be placed on Council's website and public exhibition seeking community feedback for a period of 28 days; and
  6. Require the final documents to be presented to Council at the December 2024 ordinary meeting with a report detailing community feedback received and any proposed changes to the drafts for consideration by Council and adoption of a final set of plans.
    Appendix 1a)
    The engineering Department operations be reviewed to deliver significant productivity increases. Indoor staff to be reorganised to deliver productivity increases.
    The Planning department structure and operations be reviewed by a taskforce of GM or Deputy GM, Director Planning Place and Sustainability and 3 Councillors.
    Review of non essential assets and progress a plan for disposal, lease or transfer to community stewardship.
    The GM's KPI be linked to Federation Councils progress on these points.
(Lost)

  1.  THAT Council note the report on Additional Motions for 2024 Local Government NSW Conference; and
  2. THAT Council endorse the following additional motions for submission to the 2024  Local Government NSW Annual Conference:
    1. THAT Local Government NSW calls on the NSW Electoral Commission to review the information and procedures for candidates nominating for Local Government Elections.

  4. THAT Local Government NSW lobby the NSW State Government to review the waste minimisation legislation in regards to improving the situation for regional and rural landholders; and

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"The Mayor, Councillor Cheryl Cook and Councillor Susan Wearne left the meeting at 9:38 AM.

Deputy Mayor, Councillor Rowena Black occupied the Chair.

Alternate Motion
MOVED on the motion of Councillor Derek Schoen
  1. THAT Council receive and note the contents of the report Development Application 10.2023.210.1 – Drive Thru Bottle Shop and associated carparking, landscaping and signage;
  2. THAT Council refuse to grant Development Consent to Development Application 20.2023.210.1 for a Drive Thru Bottle Shop and associated carparking, landscaping and signage in accordance  with section 4.16(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 for the following reasons: 
    1. The additional traffic generated by the proposed drive thru bottle shop and the proposed vehicle access and egress onto Sturt Street, coupled with existing traffic volumes in the area will have a detrimental impact on the efficiency of the local road network and pedestrian safety in the vicinity of the site. Therefore the proposal is  contrary to the provisions of Section 4.15(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.
    2. The development would have detrimental social amenity impacts for the township, and is therefore contrary to the provisions of Section 4.15(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.
    3. The proposed development has generated a notable volume of public submissions and concerns and approval would not be in the public interest, resulting in the development being contrary Section 4.15(d) and (e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.
  3. THAT Council advise Transport for NSW and Essential Energy of the determination of this application; and
  4. THAT Council advise all submitters of the determination made by Council.
There was no seconder and the motion lapsed.

298/2024FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and David Harrison
  1. THAT Council receive and note the contents of the report Development Application 10.2023.210.1 - Drive Thru Bottle Shop and associated carparking, landscaping and signage at 86-96 Sturt Street Howlong;
  2. THAT Council grant Development Consent to Development Application 10.2023.210.1 for a Drive Thru Bottle Shop and associated carparking, landscaping and signage at 86-96 Sturt Street Howlong (Lot 18 DP1295216) subject to the conditions contained in the DRAFT Notice of Determination attached to this Agenda;
  3. THAT Council advise Transport for NSW and Essential Energy of the determination of this application; and
  4. THAT Council advise all submitters of the determination made by Council.
(Carried)

Voting
For: Councillors Rowena Black, David Bott, Patrick Bourke, David Harrison, Andrew Kennedy and Richard Nixon.
Against: Councillor Derek Schoen.

The Mayor, Councillor Cheryl Cook and Councillor Susan Wearne returned to the meeting at 9:51 AM.

353/2024FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Richard Nixon and Rowena Black
  1. THAT Council acknowledges that the current, proposed redevelopment plan for Albury hospital continues to fall critically short of meeting the current and future health needs of the Albury Wodonga Regional Community;
  2. THAT Council supports the development of a fully funded, new, single site hospital in a new central cross-border location, for the Albury Wodonga region, that meets the health points of care requirements as identified in the 2021 Albury Wodonga Health Clinical Services Plan;
  3. THAT Council calls on the State Governments of Victoria and New South Wales to pause the current redevelopment plans for the Albury Hospital, and redirect efforts towards a fully funded, new single-site hospital in Albury or Wodonga;
  4. THAT Council calls upon the Australian Government and the State Governments of Victoria and New South Wales to collaborate for the provision of a fully funded, health service that meets the current and future needs of all the regional communities within the catchment of Albury Wodonga Health;
  5. THAT Council urgently seeks assurances from the New South Wales and Victorian State Governments to allay the fears of our community that the $558 million investment allocated to the Albury Wodonga Health Service is committed regardless of the form the new hospital may take;
  6. THAT Council urgently seeks commitment from the State Governments of Victoria and New South Wales to provide interim solutions to address the current, ongoing hospital capacity deficiencies, including but not limited to:
    1. Additional beds (like modular wards) now that have operational staffing; and
    2. Additional theatres now funded to operate effectively; and
    3. Capital and operational funding to meet the above short-term needs;
  7. THAT Council authorises the GM and Mayor to
    1. Advocate for, and communicate this position statement with the State Governments of Victoria and New South Wales, the Federal Government, and with the Board of Albury-Wodonga Health;
    2. Use the Council’s communication channels, including but not limited to website, social media channels, and newsletters to inform the community;
  8. THAT Council authorises the GM and Mayor to
    1. Advocate for Regional Boundary Changes, and specifically that the current proposed Hume Region be split into two regions and that Albury Wodonga Health run the Ovens Murray Local Health Service Network as the Health Community of Interest emanating from Albury Wodonga Region;
    2. Participate in any meeting requested of the regional Mayors with the Victorian and NSW Premiers, Health Ministers, Cross Border Commissioners and the Prime Minister, and Australian Government Health Minister;
    3. Provide support through media release and socials - noting the Mayors have met and expressed concern around formation of local health service networks, concern about maintaining local decision making and the impact these decisions may have on providing an effective health service in the Albury Wodonga Region.
  9. THAT Council receive a report at the January 2025 Council Meeting on the Health position paper tabled by the Regional Business Chamber to formally consider adoption of the paper including with any amendments proposed by Council and agreed to by the Chamber.
(Carried)

Councillor Derek Schoen foreshadowed a motion if the above motion was unsuccessful, being to remove the word "new" from item 2 & 3 and leave all else as is.  As the motion was carried, this foreshadowed motion did not therefore proceed to seeking a seconder and being debated.

14/2025FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Patrick Bourke
  1. THAT Council notes the report on the exhibition of the revised Long Term Financial Plan for 2024-2034;
  2. THAT Council acknowledges and considers the four submissions received during the public exhibition period;
  3. THAT Council endorses the following recommended changes to the exhibited revised Long Term Financial Plan for 2024-2034:
    • add section with narrative providing a summary of the risk assessment and referring to the appendix for more information;  
    • add the risk assessment of the Special Rate Variation (SRV) options, as presented to Council in November 2024, as an appendix to the LTFP;
    • minor grammar changes identified to improve readability;
    • remove change in service level in Year 2 onwards relating to the decreased subsidy to Service NSW in section 5 to reflect Councils decision in the July 2024 Council meeting to maintain the current service level; and update asset ratios in section 10 for a more holistic representation of the relationship between the SRV and investment in Council assets.
  4. THAT Council adopts the exhibited revised Long Term Financial Plan for 2024-2034 with the above endorsed changes and publish on Council's website; and
  5. THAT Council adopts the exhibited Delivery Program 2023-2026 and Operational Plan 2024-2025 with the above endorsed changes and publish on Council's website.
(Carried)

50/2025FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Susan Wearne
  1. THAT Council endorse the allocation of insurance funds, subject to approval and release of funds by the insurer, as follows:
    1. $460,000 to the Corowa Civic Centre to relocate amenities to the 1st floor and abandoned the flood prone basement;

(Carried)

    1. Rates and Charges - Hire Prices for Urana Courthouse Museum. Note from staff - Advise the Committee that Fees and Charges are recommended by the Committee and required to be adopted by Council as per the NSW Local Government Act 1993 - staff to liaise with the Committee to ensure their recommendations are included in the draft fees and charges presented to Council for exhibition, and ultimately the final charges adopted at the June Council meeting.  
    2. Urana Cemetery Seating - Suggest need for more seating and looking into funding through Local Member. Note from staff - The Committee will liaise with staff on this proposed project, no objection in principle with the Committee assisting Council with seeking funding for this. 
    3. Large Solar Battery for town at Victoria Park - Note/Update from staff - Committee to provide Council with further information.
    4. Electric Charging Station in Urana - NSW Government has incentive programs but there are additional costs. Committee suggests Anna Street across from Cafe. Note from staff - Council has a resolution not to accept any Charging Stations on Council land due to ongoing costs of managing these - Committee to be advised.
(Carried)

10.4. Development Application 10.2024.115.1 (PAN-467681) - Alterations and additions to 2 transportable dwellings and use as dual occupancy - 79 Hume Street Mulwala

Councillor Patrick Bourke left the meeting at 10:20 AM.
Councillor Patrick Bourke returned to the meeting at 10:21 AM.

Adjournment of Meeting
RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Susan Wearne
THAT the meeting be adjourned for morning tea at 10:21 AM.

The morning tea break was held earlier than the usual 10:30 AM time to allow some minor audio issues to be rectified with the live stream.


Resumption of Meeting
RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Derek Schoen
THAT the meeting resumed at 10:50 AM with all Councillors present.

Staff Recommendation
  1. THAT Council receive and note the contents of this report; and
  2. THAT Council refuse to grant development consent to Development Application 10.2024.115.1 (PAN-467681) proposing alterations and additions to 2 x Transportable Dwellings to be installed on the site for use as a Dual Occupancy development, for the following reasons:
1.  The proposed development is inconsistent with Objective 1.3(g) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 in that the development does not promote good design and does not provide for suitable amenity for future residents and neighbouring properties
2.  The proposed development is contrary to section 4.15(1)(a)(ii) Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 in that the development is inconsistent with Corowa Development Control Plan 2013, specifically the objectives and requirements of Chapter 2.1 Character of the area; Chapter 2.2 Streetscape and Chapter 2.7 Landscaping.
3.  The proposed development is contrary to section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 in that it is considered incompatible with the local built environment when taking into consideration the design of the proposal.
4.  The proposed development is contrary to section 4.15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 in that is not considered to be in the public interest to approve development which is inconsistent with the adopted policies and legislation which aim to promote the appropriate development of land and to promote good design and suitable amenity for future residents and neighbouring properties.

Motion lapsed as there was no mover or seconder.

Alternate motion
  MOVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Patrick Bourke
  1. THAT Council receive and note the contents of this report; and
  2. THAT Council grant development consent to Development Application 10.2024.115.1 (PAN-467681) proposing alterations and additions to 2 x Transportable Dwellings to be installed on the site for use as a Dual Occupancy development.

Motion was withdrawn after debate due to Council considering conditions needed to be added to any approval and none were prepared by staff at this point other than the refusal conditions submitted with the staff recommendation.

RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Patrick Bourke
THAT Council defer report 10.4 until later in the meeting to allow suitable approval conditions to be considered by Council.
(Carried)

94/2025FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Richard Nixon
  1. THAT Council receive and note the contents of this report; and
  2. THAT Council grant development consent to Development Application 10.2024.115.1 for Alterations and additions to 2 transportable buildings and use as a dual occupancy at Lot 6 Sec 11 DP758726, 79 Hume Street MULWALA NSW 2647, subject to the conditions detailed below:

GENERAL CONDITIONS

  1. Approved plans and supporting documentation
Development must be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and documents, except where the conditions of this consent expressly require otherwise.
Approved plans

In the event of any inconsistency between the approved plans and documents, the approved plans prevail. In the event of any inconsistency with the approved plans and a condition of this consent, the condition prevails. (GEN001)
Reason: To ensure all parties are aware of the approved plans and supporting documentation that applies to thedevelopment.
  1. Advice on further approvals
The landowner’s attention is drawn to the need to obtain separate approval for any ancillary activity not approved by this consent, including, but not limited to:
  • A Section 68 Application must be submitted and approved for installation of the transportable dwellings on the site;
  • A Section 68 Application must be submitted and approved for all plumbing and drainage work;
  • An approval under Section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 must be submitted and approved for any work within a road reserve, including driveway construction;
  • A Construction Certificate for any building work, accompanied by plans and documents which demonstrate compliance with the current version of the Building Code of Australia and National Construction Code.
  • A water connection application form for separate water supply connections to each dwelling must be submitted to, and approved by, Federation Council. (GEN002)
Reason: To ensure compliance with related legislation.
  1. Construction certificate plans
A construction certificate is required under section 6.7 of the Act. All plans and documentation to be prepared and/or updated shall demonstrate full compliance with the National Construction Code (NCC) prior to submitting the application for a construction certificate. 
No building work shall commence on the site without first obtaining the granting and issue of a Construction Certificate. (GEN007)
Reason: To ensure that all construction is in accordance with required standards and approvals.
  1. National Construction Code
The buildings and structures shall be designed and constructed in accordance with the relevant documents applicable under the National Construction Code. This may include:
1. Building Code of Australia (BCA), Volume 1.
2. Building Code of Australia (BCA), Volume 2.
3. ABCB Housing Provisions Standard.
4. Plumbing Code of Australia (PCA), Volume 3. (GEN008)
Reason: To ensure that all construction is in accordance with required standards and approvals.
  1. Occupation certificate
The building (or part thereof) shall not be used or occupied until: 
  1. It is completed in accordance with the relevant approvals and an Occupation Certificate and/or Final Completion Certificate is granted; or
  2. The Council issues written authorisation to allow occupancy or use prior to completion. (GEN009)
Reason: To ensure buildings are completed in accordance with all approvals and fit for occupancy.
  1. Before starting Building and Construction Work
Prior to commencing any building construction works, the following provisions of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 are to be complied with:
  1. A Construction Certificate (CC) is to be obtained in accordance with Section 6.7 of the Act.
  2. A Certifier has been appointed as the Principal Certifier and the appointment has been made be by the person having the benefit of the development consent or other person authorised by the regulations. The Council is to be notified of the appointment in accordance with Section 6.6 of the Act.
  3. Council is to be notified at least two (2) days in advance of the intention to commence building works in accordance with Section 6.6 of the Act.
  4. The person with the benefit of the development consent, if not an owner builder, must appoint a principal contractor for the building work who is the holder of a valid contractor licence if any residential building work is involved.
  5. Submit to the Principal Certifier a copy of the Home Building Compensation Fund (HBCF) insurance certificate as required by the Home Building Act 1989, if applicable. (GEN031)
Reason: To ensure compliance with related legislation and the National Construction Code (NCC)
  1. Preservation of vegetation
No trees or shrubs on the site or on adjacent footpaths or nature strips (with the exception of those identified as being removed on the stamped plans) shall be impacted in any way during construction or site works. (GEN010)
Reason: To protect vegetation from development works.
  1. Fire and smoke alarms – manufactured/transportable homes
A manufactured/transportable home must be equipped with an automatic fire detection and alarm system that complies with the requirements of Building Code of Australia, Volume 2, Performance Requirement - H3P2 and/or Part 9.5 of the ABCB Housing Provisions in relation to Class 1 buildings within the meaning of that Code/s. When there is more than 1 smoke alarm required, the interconnection of the smoke alarms is mandatory to signal and activate all smoke alarms at the same time. (GEN026)
Reason: To protect future residents and meet applicable building standards.
  1. Compliance plate
A compliance plate must be attached to an accessible part of each of the following structures:
  1. a manufactured home;
  2. an associated structure that forms part of a manufactured home;
  3. an associated structure comprising a free-standing garage.
and must specify the following:
  • the name of the manufacturer of the manufactured home or associated structure;
  • the unique identification number for each major section of the manufactured home;
  • the month and year during which the manufactured home or associated structure was constructed;
  • the design gust wind speed for the manufactured home or associated structure;
  • a statement that the manufactured home or associated structure complies with the requirements of this Part;
  • the name of the practicing structural engineer by whom the engineer’s certificate has been issued in respect of the manufactured home.
A unique identification number must be permanently marked on each major section of the manufactured home.
A compliance plate must be designed, constructed, issued and registered in accordance with any directions in force under this clause. (GEN027)
Reason: To comply with applicable legislation.
  1. Home Building Compensation/Owner Building Permit
If you are an Owner-Builder, supply:
  • For projects valued over $10,000 an Owner-Builder Permit. 
If you are engaging a Licensed Builder:
  • For projects valued $20,000 and under, your builder’s name, address and license details.
  • For projects valued more than $20,000 a Home Building Compensation (HBCF) Insurance Certificate and the Builder’s name, address, and license details. (GEN032)
Reason: To ensure all required documentation for construction is supplied.
 

BUILDING WORK

BEFORE APPROVAL TO INSTALL TRANSPORTABLE DWELLINGS AND 

BEFORE ISSUE OF A CONSTRUCTION CERTIFICATE

  1. Design amendments
Before the issue of a Section 68 Approval for installation of transportable dwellings, plans and specifications detail the following required amendments to the approved plans and documents:
  1. Redesign of the laundry in each dwelling with minimum circulation spaces of a laundry room to comply with the Building Code of Australia. The circulation space must not be encumbered by the door or other fixtures in the room. The laundry must have a wash tub and space for a washing machine located in the same room. 
NB: These amendments must also be included in amended plans for the Section 68 Application for Plumbing and Drainage submitted for this development. (BCC003 - Modified)
Reason: To require minor amendments to the plans endorsed by the consent authority following assessment of the development and to satisfy and comply with the minimum requirements specified in the Building Code of Australia for facilities in a dwelling.
  1. Plumbing and Drainage Approval 
Prior to the Principal Certifier issuing a relevant Construction Certificate (CC) for the development, the required Section 68 Approval/s under the Local Government Act 1993 for Plumbing and Drainage shall be granted for the development by Federation Council. (BCC016 - Modified)
Reason: To protect property and ensure adequate drainage can be provided to the site in accordance with the required standards.
  1. Erosion and sediment control plan
Before the issue of a construction certificate, an erosion and sediment control plan must be prepared by a suitably qualified person in accordance with the guidelines set out in the NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure manual Guidelines for erosion and sediment control on building sites, dated October 2024 and as amended from time to time. (BCC004)
Reason: To ensure no substance other than rainwater enters the stormwater system and waterways.
  1. Long service levy
Before the issue of the relevant construction certificate, the long service levy must be paid to the Long Service Corporation of Council under the Building and Construction industry Long Service Payments Act 1986, section 34, and evidence of the payment is to be provided to the certifier. (BCC005
Reason: To ensure the long service levy is paid.
  1. Construction management plan
A Construction Management Plan to address construction activity, access and parking, is to be prepared to ensure that suitable provision is available on site for all vehicles associated with the construction of the development to alleviate any need to park within, or load/unload from any road reserve. No storage of any material within the road reserve will be permitted at any time. Appropriate signage and fencing are to be installed and maintained to affect this requirement. (BCC002A)
Reason: To require details of measures that will protect the public, and the surrounding environment, during site works and construction.
  1. Developer contributions (Section 7.12)
The following monetary contributions are required and payable to Council in accordance with Section 7.12 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act, 1979, to provide for the increased demand for public amenities and services resulting from the development.
Purpose
Total
Section 7.12 (calculated at 1% of estimated cost of works)
$2,200.00
The amounts payable under this condition are due prior to the release of the Construction Certificate. It is the responsibility of the Principal Certifying Authority to ensure that contributions have been paid to Council in accordance with this Consent. (BCC018)
Reason: To ensure development contributes toward the cost of urban works and services. 
  1. Vehicle crossing requirements
The development must have residential vehicular crossings constructed generally in accordance with Federation Council’s Engineering Guidelines for Subdivisions and Development Standards and standard drawings. Details must be shown on the plans submitted with any Construction Certificate application and conform with the following:
  • A standard vehicular crossing shall be constructed at right angles to the road to suit the proposed driveways, and any existing redundant crossing shall be removed.
  • Any proposed vehicular crossing shall have satisfactory clearance (minimum 1.0m) to any drainage, water and sewer infrastructure, power or Telecommunications pole, manhole cover or marker, street tree or property boundary. Any relocation, alteration or replacement required shall be in accordance with the requirements of the relevant Authority and shall be at the applicant's expense.
  • The access driveways shall be paved with concrete. (BCC019)
Reason: To ensure adequate vehicular access is provided to the development as part of the construction works.

BEFORE BUILDING WORK COMMENCES

  1. Separate metered water supply and approval
Each dwelling must be provided with separate metered water supply, connected to Council’s reticulation main. The services must be installed to enable the isolation of each lot and not cause inconvenience to other lots. 
Any connection to the reticulation main shall be done by Council. A water connection application form must be submitted and appropriate fees paid to Federation Council prior to the commencement of works. All works will be at cost to the applicant.  (DBW030)
Reason: To ensure water supply services are provided to each lot.
  1. Erosion and sediment controls in place
Before any site work commences the Principal Certifier must be satisfied the erosion and sediment controls in the erosion and sediment control plan are in place. These controls must remain in place until any bare earth has been restabilised in accordance with the guidelines set out in the NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure manual Guidelines for erosion and sediment control on building sites, dated October 2024 and as amended from time to time.  (BWC003)
Reason: To ensure sediment laden runoff and site debris do not impact local stormwater systems and waterways.
  1. Site sign
A sign must be erected in a prominent position on any site on which building work is being carried out:
  1. Showing the name, address and telephone number of the Principal Certifier for the work, and
  2. Showing the name of the principal contractor (if any) for any building work and a telephone number on which that person may be contacted outside working hours, and
  3. Stating that unauthorised entry to the site is prohibited.
Any such sign is to be maintained while the building work is being carried out, but must be removed when the work has been completed. (BWC015)
Reason: To provide information to the public in regard to construction works being undertaken.
  1. On site toilet facilities
On site toilet facilities for construction site staff are to be provided prior to the commencement of any works. (BWC016)
Reason: To provide for the amenity of construction workers.
 DURING BUILDING WORK
  1. Hours of work  
Building and site work must only be carried out between 7.00am and 5.00pm on Monday to Saturday and no construction is to be carried on at any time on a Sunday or Public Holiday.
Building and site work is not to be carried out outside of these times except where there is an emergency, or for urgent work directed by a police officer or a public authority. (DBW004)
Reason: To protect the amenity of the surrounding area.
  1. Construction deliveries
While building and site work is being carried out, deliveries of material and equipment must only be carried out between 7.00am and 5.00pm on Monday to Saturday and no deliveries are to occur at any time on a Sunday or Public Holiday. (BWC001 - Modified)
Reason: To protect the amenity of neighbouring properties.
  1. Procedure for critical stage inspections
While building work is being carried out, the work must not continue after each critical stage inspection unless the principal certifier is satisfied the work may proceed in accordance with this consent and the relevant construction certificate. (DBW008)
Reason: To require approval to proceed with building work following each critical stage inspection.
  1. Separate house drainage connections
During construction, each lot is to be provided with a separate and distinct house drainage service connected to Council’s sewer main, with plumbing work complying with the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 and the Section 68 Approval issued by Council. (DBW036)
Reason: To ensure each lot is provided with separate services which enable isolation from each other.
  1. Responsibility for changes to public infrastructure
While site work is being carried out, any costs incurred as a result of the approved removal, relocation or reconstruction of infrastructure (including ramps, footpaths, kerb and gutter, light poles, kerb inlet pits, service provider pits, street trees or any other infrastructure in the street footpath area) are the responsibility of the person with the benefit of the consent. (DBW009)
Reason: To ensure payment of approved changes to public infrastructure.
  1. No use of public land
The nature strip/footpath/roadway shall not be used for the storage of building materials i.e., sand, bricks, timber etc.  The public land outside the property is to be maintained in its original condition to enable safe pedestrian access past the site at all times. (DBW017)
Reason: To protect public roads and road reserves and provide safe pedestrian movement.
  1. Sanitary plumbing and drainage
All sanitary plumbing and drainage work shall only be carried out by a licensed plumber and drainer and no work is to be covered over or concealed from view until it has been inspected. (DBW018)
Reason: To ensure compliance with related legislation.
  1. Stormwater and surface water
All stormwater and surface water shall be collected and piped to a lawful point of discharge as by the determined Council. The carrying out of earthworks and/or building works on the site shall not direct water on to or cause nuisance to adjoining properties. (DBW019)
Reason: To protect buildings and neighbouring properties from stormwater and surface water.
  1. Termite protection
Consideration may need to be given to providing termite barriers to protect building contents or stored materials from termites.  This is particularly important in concrete slab floors with construction or control joints. (DBW020)
Reason: To protect buildings and building contents from termites.
  1. Works within a road reserve
All works within the road reserve, which includes the area between the Property boundary and the roadway, require approval under section 138 of the Roads Act. 
The applicant shall submit the following details to Council for approval prior to any work being undertaken in the road reserve:
  • A Current Public Liability certificate with a minimum cover of $20 Million (AUD)
  • A site plan of the works to be undertaken
  • A certified Traffic Control Plan for the proposed works, prepared by an TfNSW accredited holder of ‘Prepare Work Zone Traffic Management Plan’ qualification. (DBW021)
Reason: To manage works within a road reserve.
  1. Damage or disturbance to road reserve
Any damage or disturbance to the road reserve is to be restored to match surrounding landform in accordance with Council requirements. Any redundant vehicular access points to the subject site from Steel Street shall be removed and the road reserve and kerb and gutter reinstated to match the surrounding roadside landform in accordance with Council requirements. (DBW028)
Reason: To ensure public assets are repaired if damaged during works on the site.
  1. Environmental Impact
The activities and use of site/ building and/or structure) shall be undertaken in such a way as to not interfere with the amenity of the locality by reason of the emission of noise, vibration, smell, fumes, smoke, vapour, steam, ash, soot, dust, waste water, waste products or grit, oil or otherwise. (DBW022)
Reason: To protect the amenity of the local area and the environment.
BEFORE ISSUE OF AN OCCUPATION CERTIFICATE
  1. Removal of waste upon completion
Before the issue of an occupation certificate, all refuse, spoil and material unsuitable for use on-site must be removed from the site and disposed of at an approved waste management facility. (BOO006)
Reason: To ensure waste material is appropriately disposed and the site is cleared of all waste materials.
  1. Repair of infrastructure
Before the issue of an occupation certificate:
  1. any public infrastructure damaged as a result of the carrying out of work approved under this consent (including damage caused by, but not limited to, delivery vehicles, waste collection, contractors, sub-contractors, concreting vehicles) must be fully repaired to the written satisfaction of council, and at no cost to council, or
  2. if the works in (a) are not carried out to council’s satisfaction, council may carry out the works required and the costs of any such works must be paid as directed by council and in the first instance will be paid using the security deposit required to be paid under this consent. (BOO007)
Reason: To ensure any damage to public infrastructure is rectified.
  1. Driveway and parking area sealing
All internal driveways and parking areas and access to the property shall be sealed in an all weather material approved by the Council. (BOO009)
Reason: To provide for adequate and safe vehicular access.
  1. Completion of landscape works
Before the issue of an occupation certificate, the principal certifier must be satisfied all landscape have been completed in accordance with approved plans and documents and any relevant conditions of this consent. (BOO001)
Reason: To ensure the approved landscaping works have been completed in accordance with the approved landscaping plan(s).
  1. Street Number for Property Identification 
A street number shall be displayed in a prominent location at the front of the property in the interest of public safety and the delivery of goods, parcels and emergency services. (BOO034)
Reason: To ensure the property can be easily identified.
  1. Completion of Plumbing and Drainage
Before the issue of an Occupation Certificate the responsible plumbing contractor is to submit to Council a Certificate of Compliance (COC) and a works as constructed Sewer Service Diagram (SSD) following a satisfactory result from the final plumbing and drainage inspection at the property/site. All plumbing and drainage work is to comply with the relevant legislation and granted approvals issued under Section 68 of the Local Government Act 1993. (BOO044)
Reason: To ensure compliance with the relevant legislation.

General advisory notes

This consent contains the conditions imposed by the consent authority which are to be complied with when carrying out the approved development. However, this consent is not an exhaustive list of all obligations which may relate to the carrying out of the development under the EP&A Act, EP&A Regulation and other legislation. Some of these additional obligations are set out in the Conditions of development consent: advisory notes. The consent should be read together with the Conditions of development consent: advisory notes to ensure the development is carried out lawfully.
The approved development must be carried out in accordance with the conditions of this consent. It is an offence under the EP&A Act to carry out development that is not in accordance with this consent. 
Building work or subdivision work must not be carried out until a construction certificate or subdivision works certificate, respectively, has been issued and a principal certifier has been appointed. 
A document referred to in this consent is taken to be a reference to the version of that document which applies at the date the consent is issued, unless otherwise stated in the conditions of this consent. 

Dictionary

The following terms have the following meanings for the purpose of this determination (except where the context clearly indicates otherwise): 
Approved plans and documents means the plans and documents endorsed by the consent authority, a copy of which is included in this notice of determination. 
AS means Australian Standard published by Standards Australia International Limited and means the current standard which applies at the time the consent is issued. 
Building work means any physical activity involved in the erection of a building. 
Certifier means a council or a person that is registered to carry out certification work under the Building and Development Certifiers Act 2018.
Construction certificate means a certificate to the effect that building work completed in accordance with specified plans and specifications or standards will comply with the requirements of the EP&A Regulation and Environmental Planning and Assessment (Development Certification and Fire Safety) Regulation 2021. 
Council means Federation Council. 
Court means the Land and Environment Court of NSW.
EPA means the NSW Environment Protection Authority.
EP&A Act means the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979. 
EP&A Regulation means the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2021. 
Independent Planning Commission means Independent Planning Commission of New South Wales constituted by section 2.7 of the EP&A Act.
Occupation certificate means a certificate that authorises the occupation and use of a new building or a change of building use for an existing building in accordance with this consent.
Principal certifier means the certifier appointed as the principal certifier for building work or subdivision work under section 6.6(1) or 6.12(1) of the EP&A Act respectively. 
Site work means any work that is physically carried out on the land to which the development the subject of this development consent is to be carried out, including but not limited to building work, subdivision work, demolition work, clearing of vegetation or remediation work.
Stormwater drainage system means all works and facilities relating to: 
the collection of stormwater, 
the reuse of stormwater, 
the detention of stormwater, 
the controlled release of stormwater, and 
connections to easements and public stormwater systems. 
Strata certificate means a certificate in the approved form issued under Part 4 of the Strata Schemes Development Act 2015 that authorises the registration of a strata plan, strata plan of subdivision or notice of conversion.
Subdivision certificate means a certificate that authorises the registration of a plan of subdivision under Part 23 of the Conveyancing Act 1919. 
Subdivision works certificate means a certificate to the effect that subdivision work completed in accordance with specified plans and specifications will comply with the requirements of the EP&A Regulation.
Sydney district or regional planning panel means Southern Regional Planning Panel.
(Carried)

74/2025FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and Susan Wearne
  1. THAT Council note the report on the Resolutions completed and progressed since the last meeting; and
  2. THAT Council rescind the following resolutions as they are no longer considered necessary to being pursued or are in part already actioned -  
  1. 95/15 - 
    i)  That Council note the report on the Billabidgee Aged Care Units;
    iii) That Council re-engage with NSW Family and Community Services, Argyle Housing, Homes Out West and Lutheran Aged Care to discuss options for the units during 2015/2016;
    iv) That Council, from existing building reserves continue design and costing investigations for converting two (2) units into a single two (2) bedroom unit configuration as well as upgrading at least one (1) existing unit to current accessible standards;
    v) That Council engage with service providers to investigate options to better market the availability of the units to the wider community.
  2. 99/17FC - "99/17FC RESOLVED that: 
    1. Council note the report on Integrated Planning and Reporting incorporating the 10-year Financial Plan, Delivery Program 2017 to 2020 and Operational Plan 2017-2018. 
    2. In accordance with Section 405 of the Local Government Act 1993 Council adopts the Integrated Planning and Reporting incorporating the:  
    a. 10 year Financial Plan, Delivery Program 2017 to 2020 and Operational Plan 2017-2018.  
    b. The 2017-2018 Revenue Policy and Fees & Charges inclusive of the Riverina Regional Library Fees and Charges.  
    c. The variations as detailed in this report and attachments, including any other changes as resolved at this meeting. 
    3. Council authorise the signing and affixing of the Seal of the Council to all Loan Documents relating to 2017-2018 loan funding as detailed in the Federation Council Operational Plan 2017-2018 and Budget. 
    4. That Council officers prepare a review of the cost contributions of user and service levels of the recreation facilities across Federation Council."
  3. 109/17FC RESOLVED that Council investigate the cost of erecting a flagpole for the Indigenous flag at the Corowa Civic Centre.
  4. 06/18FC RESOLVED on the motion of Whitechurch and Wales that:
    1. The letter and petition from Michael Robson objecting to the closure of Stephen Street, Urana to vehicles longer than 15 metres, be received and noted.
    2. Council receive a further report on this matter."
  5. 216/18FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Miegel and Longley: 
    1. THAT Council not pay compensation for electricity and maintenance; and 
    2. THAT Council develop and implement a Compensation Policy for User Groups prior to making any further decisions of this nature.
  6. 236/19FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Whitechurch and Longley that Council investigate the interest from Melbourne based councils with a view of forming a sister city relationship, and a further report be presented to council on this.
  7. 362/19FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Thomas and Longmire:  1. THAT Federation Council in consultation with the Federation Council Rural Working Group make a submission to the Legislative Assembly Committee Inquiry into Support for Drought Affected Communities in NSW: and  2. THAT the submission highlight the urgent need for potable water supply to the rural communities of Balldale and Daysdale and Council seek State Government Funding.
  8. 79/20FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Wales and Thomas:
     1. THAT Council note the report on the unsuccessful grant application for the Lake Urana Precinct, under the NSW State Government Regional Growth Environment and Tourism Fund (Round Two – Stream One); and 
    2. THAT Council receive further reports on the Lake Urana Precinct Project as opportunities present for future funding.
  9. 313/20FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Longley and Whitechurch:
    1. THAT Council endorse the Corowa Swimming Pool Advisory Committee’s recommendation on the naming of the new facility ‘Corowa Aquatic Centre’;
    2. THAT Council work with the Corowa Swimming Pool Advisory Committee to design an Honour Board and receive further reports as this progresses, with this process not to delay any progress towards the official opening of the new facility; and
    3. THAT Council at a later stage consider if the Individual Pools should be named, including further consulting with the family members of any suggested names and the Corowa Swimming Pool Advisory Committee.
  10. 380/20FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Thomas and Miegel that Council ask staff to provide a report in respect to community needs in planning future housing estates.
(Carried)

    1. Confirm that the prior adoption of the Corowa, Howlong and Mulwala Flood Study (Final Report October 2024) by Resolution 323/2024FC in November 2024 does not alter the defined Flood Planning Area as recorded in the maps to the LEP, subject to any higher level registered in title;
    2. Will rely upon the Flood Planning Area defined in the Corowa Local Environmental Plan 2012 (LEP) until such time that the Flood Risk Management Study and Plan (FRMS&P) have been completed and adopted by Council, or such other time as further information is available to Council in order to form a definitive position on the adoption of amended 1% AEP flood levels;
    3. Will give consideration to the Corowa, Howlong and Mulwala Flood Study when assessing any applications lodged under the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 and the Local Government Act 1993 in the context of the suitability of the site for development pursuant to section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act and section 733 of the Local Government Act 1993;
    4. Delegate to its General Manager to seek engagement from all key stakeholders in the Flood Risk Management Study and Plan (FRMS&P) process, including relevant water authorities, to investigate opportunities to mitigate flood risk to all impacted areas within the Federation Local Government Area;
    5. Utilise Advisory Notes within all relevant determinations to ensure that applicants are aware of the Corowa, Howlong and Mulwala Flood Study and risks associated with utilising the  1% AEP flood level prescribed in existing LEP maps pending the completion of the Flood Risk Management Process which may alter the 1% AEP flood level;

    6. Will continue to provide clear and up to date information to current and future owners of property and individuals seeking information from Council, via planning certificates or otherwise, in relation to flooding. This is to include a reference to the Flood Study and the known differential in the 1% AEP flood levels between the current LEP maps and the maps and levels established by the Flood Study thus enabling recipients to make an informed decision whether to accept risk, if any, during the intervening period until the Flood Risk Management Process has been completed.
(Carried)

169/2025FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and Susan Wearne
  1. THAT Council note the Corowa, Howlong and Mulwala Flood Risk Management Study and Plan Tender Assessment Tender Number 2025-229
  2. THAT Council review the makeup of the Corowa, Howlong and Mulwala Flood Risk Management Committee by
    1. confirm existing community members are willing to stay on the Corowa, Howlong and Mulwala Flood Risk Management Committee.
    2. seek expressions of interest for additional community members to ensure there are 2 committee members from each town  and a representative from HCPA, SMAG, MPA and Corowa Chamber of Commerce on the Flood Risk Management Committee.
    3. At the close of the Expression of interest period that a report outlining the preferred members be prepared for Council.
    4. That the successful tenderer is able to display that they are able to engage to obtain suitable river data and flood mitigation protocols from river operators.
  1. THAT Council defer the remainder of this report to the closed session of Council under Section 10A (2) of the Local Government Act and Clause 14.1 of Council’s Code of Meeting Practice as the matters and information to be discussed contain the following: 
(d) commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed-
(i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
(ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
(iii) reveal a trade secret.

(Carried)

189/2025FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Patrick Bourke and Andrew Kennedy
  1. THAT Council receive and note the report on the community feedback on the Future Federation 2040: Community Strategic Plan (25/10046);
  2. THAT Council note and consider the 12 submissions received from community members;
  3. THAT Council endorse the following changes to the Future Federation 2040: Community Strategic Plan (25/10046):
    • Creation of a separate IP&R Framework document to alleviate the requirement for this information to be repeated in each of the IP&R documents. Thus, the section on the IP&R Framework is removed from the CSP.
    • Formatting changes to improve the presentation and readability of the document.
    • Amend content of the Financial Sustainability section to align with the recent Special Rate Variation decision by the Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal.
    • Simplify Community Engagement section to improve readability based on community feedback. 
    • Add population forecast for 2040 and factors on how the population will change to understand the community’s future needs.
    • Add percentages and number of respondents to the Strengths and Challenges to provide the community with transparency on the survey responses, as per community feedback.
    • Add target to CSP Objective 5 – Satisfaction with the performance of Council across all areas of responsibility.  Target missing from draft version. 
  4. THAT a report be presented to Council at the 30 June 2025 extraordinary meeting for consideration of Council and endorsement of the final Future Federation 2040: Community Strategic Plan.

(Carried)

Live Streaming of Council Meetings
Federation Council wishes to advise members of the public that Council meetings will be recorded and will be available after each meeting on Council’s website www.federationcouncil.nsw.gov.au 
 
All care will be taken to maintain the privacy of those in attendance, however as a visitor in the public gallery, your presence may be recorded. By remaining in the public gallery, it is assumed your consent is given in the event your image is broadcast. This includes any filming by television cameras if attendance is approved by the General Manager or Mayor.

Statement of ethical obligations

MOVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and David Bott
  1. THAT Council notes the report on the rating structure for the 2025/26 financial year;
  2. THAT Council acknowledges and considers the submissions and online surveys received during the public exhibition period;

Live Streaming of Council Meetings

Statement of ethical obligations

  1. THAT Council receive and note the minutes of the Urana Progress Association Committee Annual General Meeting dated 6 August 2025 (25/30922);
  2. THAT Council receive and note the minutes of the Urana Progress Association Committee General Meeting dated 6 August 2025 (25/30923);
  3. THAT Council note the matters raised of the Urana Progress Association Committee minutes dated 6 August 2025 and note the responses to be provided:
    1. Donation of $100 to Urana Community Bowling Club - advise Committee they do not have a delegation to donate money to other organisations and work with Committee to educate on financial management matters, and update delegations/terms of reference for Council to refresh delegations to the Committee.
    2. Welcome pack - note the Committee is developing a Urana Welcome pack, and advise the Committee if they are unaware, that Council has a new resident kit (booklet) available on the website and hardcopies may also be available)
    3.   4. THAT Council endorse the office bearers:
    • President: Barry Paterson 
    • Vice President: Wanda Oram-Miles 
    • Secretary: Wendy Mallon
    • Treasurer: Joan Field
(Carried)

9.4            Ball Park Caravan Park - Seeking endorsement of tender approach
MOVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and David Harrison
THAT Council, pursuant to Section 55 of the Local Government Act 1993 (NSW) and Clauses 166(b) and 168 of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 (NSW):
  1. Approve the use of the Selective Tendering via Expressions of Interest (EOI) method for the securing of a long term lessee for the operation and redevelopment of the Ball Park Caravan Park.
  2. Authorise the General Manager to publish a public advertisement seeking Expressions of Interest for the proposed contract in accordance with Clause 168(1).
  3. Receive a further report following the Expressions of Interest process, to consider if Council wishes to subsequently invite tenders from the applicants who are deemed best capable of fulfilling the requirements of the proposed contract, following the EOI assessment process.

Motion was Withdrawn.

MOVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and David Bott
THAT Council pause the EOI process in relation to the Ball Park Caravan Park long term management and redevelopment, and invite Reflections to present options to Council, after which time Council can accept this model, or alternatively go back to the EOI process.

Motion was Withdrawn.

RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and Rowena Black
THAT Council defer this report to seek further advice on the timeline for Reflections to present to Council and consider later in this agenda.
(Carried)

Adjournment of Meeting
RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Bott and David Harrison
THAT the meeting be adjourned for morning tea at 10:53 AM.


Resumption of Meeting
RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and Susan Wearne

331/2025FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Richard Nixon and Patrick Bourke
  1. THAT Council receive and note the minutes of the Oaklands Town Improvement Committee Annual General Meeting dated 17 September 2025 (25/36896);
  2. THAT Council note the matters raised of the Oaklands Town Improvement Committee minutes dated 17 September 2025;
  3. THAT Council:
    • disband the Oaklands Town Improvement Committee effective immediately;
    • rescind all current and previous Council delegations to the Oaklands Town Improvement Committee;
    • internally restrict monies currently attributed to the Oaklands Town Improvement Committee ($18,750.73) for future Council functions or actions that benefit the Oaklands community with consultation to be undertaken with the Oaklands community including the Oaklands Hall and Oaklands Recreation Ground Committees;
    • express its gratitude for the significant contribution made by Oaklands community members in operating this committee over many years; and
    • transfer the $3,000 annual allocation for 2025/26 to the 2025/26 Community Grants Program.
    • note that the Oaklands Swimming Pool section 355 committee is also inactive.
(Carried)

374/2025FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Bott and Derek Schoen
  1. THAT Council endorse placing the draft Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Protocols with the following amendments and place on public exhibition for 28 days;
    1. (P. 6) Subheading “Inclusion of a Welcome to Country”
      • Amend the first sentence to read ….
        Consideration should be given to the inclusion of a Welcome to Country ceremony, however any such ceremony must first be approved by an adopted Council resolution. If a Council resolution is not forthcoming, an Acknowledgment of Country shall instead be offered at the following:
    2. (P. 10) Subheading “ Inclusion of an Acknowledgement of Country”
      • Amend the first bullet point to read ….
        All formal Ordinary and Extraordinary Meetings of the Council; excluding any and all Committees of Council that are not open to the public or live streamed.
      • Delete the 5th bullet point. (From 1 Jan 2026, Council run workshops will be prohibited).
      • Third bullet point amended from owner to custodian.
    3. (P. 16) 13. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Flags
      • Amend the first paragraph to read ….
        Council will, on specific occasions, fly the Aboriginal Flag and the Torres Strait Islander Flag to demonstrate respect and to foster reconciliation and community partnership. We recognise their unique cultures and historical connection across this region.
      • Amend the second paragraph to read ….
        Council commits to exclusively fly the Australian flag within the Council Chamber during official sessions and on all flagpoles located across the Federation Council area. 
  2. THAT Council receives a further report at a future Council meeting to consider the adoption of the final copy of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Protocols.
(Carried)

MOVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and Andrew Kennedy
THAT Council develop a Working from Home (WHF) Policy.
(Lost)

Councillors Schoen, Bott and Nixon requested their vote for this motion be recorded.

Note from General Manager in finalising minutes - Council's Code of Meeting (clause 11.6) states - 11.6 If a councillor who has voted against a motion put at a council meeting so requests, the general manager must ensure that the councillor’s dissenting vote is recorded in the council’s minutes.

Whilst in the above defeated motion, the Councillors who requested their vote be recorded, actually voted ‘for’ the motion, and clause 11.6 only deals with ‘against’ votes, given the Mayor advised the Councillors she would allow this, the Councillors names who voted for the defeated motion, are therefore recorded.

354/2025FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and David Bott
  1. THAT Council notes the contents of the presentation provided by Reflections Holiday Parks (NSW Crown Holiday Parks Land Manager) regarding their operational model and their preliminary findings with regards to the potential management and redevelopment of the Ball Park Caravan Park under Reflections Holidays Parks; and
  2. THAT Council pass a further resolution based on the options provided or an alternative approach or variation of the options, to allow the operation and redevelopment of the Ball Park Caravan Park to progress.
(Carried)

Upon delivering their presentation and taking questions, the Reflections Holiday Park representatives left the Chamber/Meeting, whilst Council considered options in the Confidential report, and ultimately after debate, carried the following motion below -

355/2025FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and David Bott
THAT Council continue to pause the current Expression of Interest (EOI) process for the Ball Park Caravan Park; and - 
  1. Delegate the General Manager to enter into exclusive negotiations with Reflections Holiday Parks for the purpose of management and redevelopment of the Ball Park Caravan Park;

  2. Grant the exclusive negotiation period until the February 2026 Council meeting, and receive a report at the February Council Meeting, to allow Reflections Holiday Parks sufficient time to prepare and present a formal, detailed commercial proposal to Council for its final consideration.
(Carried)

Councillor Patrick Bourke requested his vote against be recorded.

Re-opening of the Meeting to Members of the Public
RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and Richard Nixon
THAT Council move to open session and report business from closed session at 10:54 AM.


Open Council    
The Chairperson advised the meeting of the resolutions passed in the closed session.

 Adjournment of Meeting
RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Harrison and Derek Schoen
THAT the meeting be adjourned for morning tea at 10:57 AM.


Resumption of Meeting
RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and Susan Wearne
THAT the meeting resumed at 11:14 AM with all Councillors present.

411/2025FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and Andrew Kennedy
  1. THAT Council note the report on progress of the Federation Council Annual Financial Statements for the year ended 30 June 2025; and
  2. THAT Council authorise the signing of the declaration, as follows:-
The General Purpose Financial Report has been prepared in accordance with:
  • The Local Government Act 1993 (as amended) and the Regulations made thereunder,
  • The Australian Accounting Standards and professional pronouncements, and
  • The Local Government Code of Accounting Practice and Financial Reporting.
To the best of our knowledge and belief, this Report:
  • Presents fairly the Council’s operating result and financial position for the year, and
  • Accords with Council’s accounting and other records.
The Special Purpose Financial Reports have been prepared in accordance with:
  • The NSW Government Policy Statement “Application of National Competition Policy to Local Government”.
  • The Office of Local Government Guidelines “Pricing & Costing for Council Businesses - A Guide to Competitive Neutrality”.
  • The Local Government Code of Accounting Practice and Financial Reporting.
  • The Department of Water and Energy Best-Practice Management of Water and Sewerage Guidelines.
To the best of our knowledge and belief, these Reports:
  • Present fairly the Operating Result and Financial Position for each of Council's declared business Activities for the year, and
  • Accord with Council’s accounting and other records.
(Carried)

Live Streaming of Council Meetings

The Mayor opened the meeting at 9:30am. 

Live Streaming of Council Meetings
Federation Council wishes to advise members of the public that Council meetings will be recorded and will be available after each meeting on Council’s website www.federationcouncil.nsw.gov.au 
 
All care will be taken to maintain the privacy of those in attendance, however as a visitor in the public gallery, your presence may be recorded. By remaining in the public gallery, it is assumed your consent is given in the event your image is broadcast. This includes any filming by television cameras if attendance is approved by the General Manager or Mayor.

Statement of ethical obligations
Councillors are reminded of their oath or affirmation of office made under section 233A of the Act, to faithfully and impartially carry out the functions, powers, authorities and discretions vested in them under the Local Government Act 1993 or any other Act to the best of their ability and judgment, and of their obligations under Council’s Code of Conduct to disclose and appropriately manage conflicts of interest.

I ask those gathered to join us now for a few moments of silence, as we reflect on our roles in this chamber. Please use this opportunity for contemplation, prayer or thought, to focus on our shared intentions to work respectfully together for the wellbeing of our whole community.

The Mayor noted the very tough few months with significant fires and acknowledged the efforts of first responders being Police, Ambulance, RFS and SES and Council staff and the impacts on loss of income. The Mayor then significantly noted the very tragic events of the last month, and asked for a minutes silence in memory of the three lives lost tragically in road accidents, including Stacey Carter, the mother of the Federation Youth Council Deputy Mayor Dayna Carter.

The Mayor noted the impact this has naturally had on the Youth Council members, and that support is being provided. The Mayor passed on Councils sincere condolences to the family and friends of all the victims and requested all stand for a minutes silence in honour of the lives lost.

The Mayor also spoke on the news of the imminent closure of the Corowa Golf Club, and noted that the General Manager has been having conversations with the Club, and the Mayor and General Manager and other Councillors will be attending the community meeting to be held tonight at the Golf Club.

THAT Council note the Mayoral Minute on some of the meetings and other engagements attended by the Mayor since the December 2025 Council meeting.
