The Mayor opened the meeting at 09:35 AM. 

Live Streaming of Council Meetings
Federation Council wishes to advise members of the public that Council meetings will be recorded and will be available after each meeting on Council’s website www.federationcouncil.nsw.gov.au 
 
All care will be taken to maintain the privacy of those in attendance, however as a visitor in the public gallery, your presence may be recorded. By remaining in the public gallery, it is assumed your consent is given in the event your image is broadcast. This includes any filming by television cameras if attendance is approved by the General Manager or Mayor.

Statement of ethical obligations
Councillors are reminded of their oath or affirmation of office made under section 233A of the Act, to faithfully and impartially carry out the functions, powers, authorities and discretions vested in them under the Local Government Act 1993 or any other Act to the best of their ability and judgment, and of their obligations under Council’s Code of Conduct to disclose and appropriately manage conflicts of interest.

I ask those gathered to join us now for a few moments of silence, as we reflect on our roles in this chamber. Please use this opportunity for contemplation, prayer or thought, to focus on our shared intentions to work respectfully together for the wellbeing of our whole community.

MOVED on the motion of Councillors Patrick Bourke and David Bott
  1. THAT Council continue to operate the Corowa Aerodrome; and
  2. THAT Council work in conjunction with user groups to create a positive cash flow outcome in the very near future.
(Lost)
 
Cr Schoen moved a procedural motion that recommended that points be dealt with seriatim (the points taken out and voted on individually) Cr Bourke seconded. The Mayor accommodated the request for voting on this matter.

60/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Harrison and Rowena Black
  1. THAT Council note the findings of the Corowa Aerodrome Service Review and Council’s Financial Review.
(Carried)

61/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Harrison and Rowena Black
  1. THAT Council establish a formal ‘Aerodrome Advisory Committee’ to lead the strategic divestment of the Corowa Aerodrome to a suitably qualified private entity who is willing to acquire and assume full responsibility for its ownership on or before 30 June 2029.   This includes operation, maintenance, renewal, regulatory compliance and all associated risks and liabilities, with no ongoing financial or operational obligation remaining with Federation Council.
(Carried)

 
62/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Harrison and Rowena Black
  1. THAT the committee shall comprise a diverse range of stakeholders, including aviation specialists, active airport users, local business representatives, the Corowa Business Chamber, council staff and elected councillors, who shall provide regular progress reports to Council.
(Carried)

63/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Harrison and Rowena Black
  1. THAT pending the Aerodrome Advisory Committee’s divestment outcome, Council will continue aerodrome operations with a revised fee structure. Effective 1 July 2026, occupancy/service charges will rise to $1,760 (68% increase) followed by 5% yearly increases. Further, the Council will introduce a $21,800 annual commercial rate for the site operator and a continued $19,816 ADF commitment.
(Carried)

The Mayor opened the meeting at 09:32 AM. 

Live Streaming of Council Meetings
Federation Council wishes to advise members of the public that Council meetings will be recorded and will be available after each meeting on Council’s website www.federationcouncil.nsw.gov.au 
 
All care will be taken to maintain the privacy of those in attendance, however as a visitor in the public gallery, your presence may be recorded. By remaining in the public gallery, it is assumed your consent is given in the event your image is broadcast. This includes any filming by television cameras if attendance is approved by the General Manager or Mayor.

Statement of ethical obligations
Councillors are reminded of their oath or affirmation of office made under section 233A of the Act, to faithfully and impartially carry out the functions, powers, authorities and discretions vested in them under the Local Government Act 1993 or any other Act to the best of their ability and judgment, and of their obligations under Council’s Code of Conduct to disclose and appropriately manage conflicts of interest.

I ask those gathered to join us now for a few moments of silence, as we reflect on our roles in this chamber. Please use this opportunity for contemplation, prayer or thought, to focus on our shared intentions to work respectfully together for the wellbeing of our whole community.

Cr Schoen foreshadowed a motion being option 4:

THAT Council defer a final decision on adopting a Protocols document to allow for formal engagement with Council’s established Reconciliation Action Plan (RAP) Working Group. This process could further define the appropriate RAP level (e.g., "Reflect" or "Innovate") and ensure that all associated protocols align with the finalised Plan and further conversations and engagement can occur with the local Aboriginal Community.
 
MOVED on the motion of Councillors David Bott and Andrew Kennedy
  1. THAT Council receive and note the report and the submissions regarding the exhibition of the draft Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Protocols; and
  2. THAT Council adopt the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Protocols version 2 - November 2025, as exhibited, which transitions traditional owner flags to "occasional" display and implements a requirement for a Council resolution to approve "Welcome to Country" ceremonies at civic events.
(Lost)

71/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and Rowena Black
  1. THAT Council receive and note the report and the submissions regarding the exhibition of the draft Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Protocols; and
  2. THAT Council defer a final decision on adopting a Protocols document to allow for formal engagement with Council’s established Reconciliation Action Plan (RAP) Working Group. This process could further define the appropriate RAP level (e.g., "Reflect" or "Innovate") and ensure that all associated protocols align with the finalised Plan and further conversations and engagement can occur with the local Aboriginal Community.
(Carried)

Councillors Patrick Bourke, Susan Wearne and David Harrison requested their vote against be recorded.

RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and David Bott

76/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Bott and Derek Schoen
  1. THAT Council note the update on the Rural Fire Service matters;
  2. THAT Council notes the draft minutes from the Federation Zone District Liaison Committee (DLC) held on 23 February 2026, and notes concerns with their lack of completeness on views stated by the General Manager in the meeting, and receives a further update after the next DLC meeting;
  3. THAT Council notes and endorses that information from this report be summarised and sent to local Member Mr Justin Clancy MP, Member for Albury, to seek assistance via the Minister for Emergency Services, in the 'De-teaming' of the Federation Zone (Berrigan and Federation Local Government Areas) from the voluntary Southern Border Team, to allow the stand-alone zone of Federation and Berrigan Councils to be ran from the Corowa RFS Centre, with no additional costs to be incurred by Federation, Berrigan, Albury and Greater Hume Councils, and with the higher level support, as should occur, to come from the South Western Area Command and any additional budget to be from the RFS/State Government;
  4. THAT Council request a formal response by way of agreement from the Rural Fire Service on the De-teaming request as a priority, so that planning can occur to ensure an improved Rural Fire Service delivery occurs for the benefit of the protection of the Berrigan and Federation Local Government areas from 1 July 2027;
  5. THAT Council in-principle support using an amount of $15,000, should there be sufficient underspend in the 2025/26 budget for the RFS operations, as currently projected, to plan for an expanded Corowa RFS Centre, to allow an additional truck parking area and the possibility of an State Emergency Service (SES) addition to the Centre and receive a further report on this post the finalisation of the 25/26 financial year; and
  6. THAT Council seek a position from the RFS in respect to the Land rover Defender registration CWS15Y, and what Council area it was originally vested in and where it should be; considering it is registered by Federation Council.
(Carried)

77/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and David Bott
THAT Council, pursuant to Section 55 of the Local Government Act 1993 (NSW) and Clauses 166(b) and 168 of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 (NSW):
  1. Approve the use of the Selective Tendering via Expressions of Interest (EOI) method for the securing of a long term (30 year subject to Ministerial consent) lessee for the operation and redevelopment of the Ball Park Caravan Park;
  2. Authorise the General Manager to publish a public advertisement seeking Expressions of Interest for the proposed contract in accordance with Clause 168(1) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 (NSW);
  3. Receive a further report following the Expressions of Interest process at the May Council Meeting, to consider if Council wishes to subsequently invite tenders from the applicants who are deemed best capable of fulfilling the requirements of the proposed contract, following the EOI assessment process; and
  4. Make the appropriate application steps to seek the approval of the NSW Government to enter into a 30 year lease for the Ball Park Caravan Park, being Crown Land, should a successful firm be agreed upon, and receive further reports as the matter progresses.
(Carried)

The Mayor opened the meeting at 09:30 AM. 

Live Streaming of Council Meetings
Federation Council wishes to advise members of the public that Council meetings will be recorded and will be available after each meeting on Council’s website www.federationcouncil.nsw.gov.au 
 
All care will be taken to maintain the privacy of those in attendance, however as a visitor in the public gallery, your presence may be recorded. By remaining in the public gallery, it is assumed your consent is given in the event your image is broadcast. This includes any filming by television cameras if attendance is approved by the General Manager or Mayor.

Statement of ethical obligations
Councillors are reminded of their oath or affirmation of office made under section 233A of the Act, to faithfully and impartially carry out the functions, powers, authorities and discretions vested in them under the Local Government Act 1993 or any other Act to the best of their ability and judgment, and of their obligations under Council’s Code of Conduct to disclose and appropriately manage conflicts of interest.

I ask those gathered to join us now for a few moments of silence, as we reflect on our roles in this chamber. Please use this opportunity for contemplation, prayer or thought, to focus on our shared intentions to work respectfully together for the wellbeing of our whole community.

105/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Derek Schoen
THAT Council endorse the allocation of the insurance funds received ($452,242) for the John Foord Oval as part of the 2022 flood insurance claim as follows:
  1. $40,000 to allow the land which the main buildings are positioned to be subdivided to allow a separate longer-term lease, including any planning, legal fees, land surveying and lease fees required;
  2. $150,000 to assist the Corowa Rutherglen Football Netball club (CRFNC) with finalising female netball changerooms funded under Stronger Country Communities Fund;
  3. $40,000 to undertake detailed design and quantity surveyor costs for a future flood-proofed clubroom facility;
  4. $205,000 to be used as a grant contribution for a future flood-proofed clubroom facility; and
  5. $17,242 to be held for project contingency or emergency works required.

106/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and Susan Wearne
  1. THAT Council note the update on the Code of Meeting Practice;
  2. THAT Council endorse the submission points, as re-produced in the background of this report, made to Local Government NSW by the General Manager and Mayor;
  3. THAT Council amend the current Federation Council Code of Meeting Practice as follows:
    1. adding the following clause after clause 4.11
      4.11A If more than the permitted number of speakers apply to speak ‘for’ or ‘against’ any item of business, the general manager or their delegate may, in consultation with the mayor or the mayor’s nominated chairperson, increase the number of speakers permitted to speak on an item of business, where they are satisfied that it is necessary to do so to allow the council to hear a fuller range of views on the relevant item of business.
    2. adding the following clause after clause 11.10
      11.10A Where a motion comprises multiple parts, a Councillor may move a procedural motion that a multi-part motion consisting of several items be considered seriatim (item-by-item). If the motion to consider seriatim is carried:
      (a) Unless determined otherwise, each item shall be debated and voted upon individually in the order in which they appear, and
      (b) Amendments may be moved to each item as it is considered, and
      (c) After all items have been dealt with, the Chairperson shall put the motion as a whole (as amended, if applicable) to the meeting for a final vote.
  4. THAT Council determine that under clause 362(2) that the above amendments are not in the opinion of Council to be substantial and so no public exhibition will occur and the Code be updated and adopted immediately, considering the changes are expected to allow for enhanced community participation and if it were the opposite, an exhibition would definitely be conducted.
(Carried)

101/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Patrick Bourke and Andrew Kennedy
  1. THAT Council notes the Country Mayors Association of NSW "Invest in Us" campaign advocating for increased Commonwealth Financial Assistance Grants to Local Governments, noting that the campaign seeks to restore the annual grants total amount distributed, to at least 1% of total Commonwealth taxation revenue annually, for local Councils across Australia;
  2. THAT the Commonwealth Government recognises the critical role Local Government plays in delivering essential services and infrastructure that underpin community wellbeing, economic vitality, and national resilience;
  3. THAT Council supports the campaign's core message: 'Invest in us so we can invest in them';
  4. THAT Council commits to participating in the campaign by:
    1. Sharing campaign materials through Council communication channels.
    2. Engaging with local media and community stakeholders to raise awareness.
    3. Lobbying Federal representatives to support the funding increase.
  5. [IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr Schoen raised the following matters:

  1. Requested an update regarding the details of the General Managers Contract renewal, and stated that the total remuneration package (TRP) has to be detailed in full in the resolution that endorsed the re-appointment.   The Deputy General Manager (DGM) responded to the request given the General Manager has a conflict of interest.  The DGM advised that there are guidelines that are required to be considered, and it is not actually stipulated that it is required in the resolution. A report is being prepared for the May meeting to update Council on this matter.

    Cr Bott also spoke in support of the request from Cr Schoen, regarding the details of the General Manager Contract renewal and in his view the TRP needs to be in the resolution. This is consistent with the information he had sourced. The DGM requested this information be forwarded and advised she will review and ensure all relevant information is included in the upcoming report to Council.

    The Mayor advised that the process was done with the assistance of Local Government NSW and whilst the decision was debated in the closed session as required, the decision to re-appoint was made pubic via reading out the motion and the increase to TRP in open session and the minutes showing this, in the same way Council reports other business from the closed sessions.

  2. Ball Park Caravan Park Tendering Update - Council was advised by the General Manager that the Expression of Interest (EOI) documentation is being finalised and is close to be be being sent out.

(Carried)

The Mayor opened the meeting at 09:30 AM. 

Live Streaming of Council Meetings
Federation Council wishes to advise members of the public that Council meetings will be recorded and will be available after each meeting on Council’s website www.federationcouncil.nsw.gov.au 
 
All care will be taken to maintain the privacy of those in attendance, however as a visitor in the public gallery, your presence may be recorded. By remaining in the public gallery, it is assumed your consent is given in the event your image is broadcast. This includes any filming by television cameras if attendance is approved by the General Manager or Mayor.

Statement of ethical obligations
Councillors are reminded of their oath or affirmation of office made under section 233A of the Act, to faithfully and impartially carry out the functions, powers, authorities and discretions vested in them under the Local Government Act 1993 or any other Act to the best of their ability and judgment, and of their obligations under Council’s Code of Conduct to disclose and appropriately manage conflicts of interest.

I ask those gathered to join us now for a few moments of silence, as we reflect on our roles in this chamber. Please use this opportunity for contemplation, prayer or thought, to focus on our shared intentions to work respectfully together for the wellbeing of our whole community.

143/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and David Harrison
  1. THAT Council notes the community submissions and feedback received on the draft Operational Plan & Annual Budget 2026/27, and Long Term Financial Plan for 2026 - 2036.
(Carried)
Councillor Derek Schoen left the meeting at 09:57am.
Councillor Derek Schoen returned to the meeting at 09:59am.
144/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Harrison and Andrew Kennedy
  1. THAT Council considers the request for the intersection upgrade at Redlands Road and Tom Roberts Road (refer to Respondent 5 - Future Federation 2026-2027 Written Community Submissions attachment) and adopt no change to 2026/27 plans given the existing proposed capital works program has been developed based on need from the recent asset condition assessment.
(Carried)

MOVED on the motion of Councillors Patrick Bourke and Andrew Kennedy
  1. THAT Council considers the request for establishing a reserve for a demerger business case and adopt no change to 2026/27 plans.
Motion was Withdrawn.

145/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Susan Wearne and Rowena Black
  1. THAT Council considers the request for establishing a reserve for a demerger business case and adopt no change to 2026/27 plans.
(Carried)
Councillor Andrew Kennedy left the meeting at 10:13am due to the conflict of interest declared.
Councillor Derek Schoen left the meeting at 10:15am.
Councillor Derek Schoen returned to the meeting at 10:17am.
146/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and Derek Schoen
  1. THAT Council considers the request for YMTB funding as detailed in Section 3 of this report and adopt no change to 2026/27 plans.
(Carried)
Councillor Patrick Bourke requested his vote against be recorded.
Councillor Andrew Kennedy returned to the meeting at 10:22am after the item was dealt with.

MOVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Richard Nixon
  1. THAT Council considers the request for limiting the general rate increase to the rate peg (refer to Respondent 4 - Future Federation 2026-2027 Written Community Submissions attachment) and adopt no change to 2026/27 plans given the proposed 11.8% increase is to be invested in roads, drainage and buildings, consistent with Council's previous commitments to the community, the recent Special Rate Variation application and the IPART approval.

Amendment to the motion
MOVED on the motion of Councillors David Bott and Derek Schoen
  1. Defer the consideration of the request from respondent 4 to the June 2026 Council Meeting following exhibition of the Revenue Policy.

The amendment was put and passed and became the motion and the motion was then put and carried.
147/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Bott and Derek Schoen
  1. Defer the consideration of the request from respondent 4 to the June 2026 Council Meeting following exhibition of the Revenue Policy.
(Carried)

148/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Susan Wearne and David Harrison
  1.  THAT Council adopts the recommended changes to the Draft Operational Plan 2026/27 (numbered 1 - 23) as detailed in Section 4 of this report.
(Carried)

RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Rowena Black and Derek Schoen

Resumption of Meeting
RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and Richard Nixon
THAT the meeting resumed at 11:11 AM with all Councillors present.

Bring forward reports
RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and Rowena Black
THAT Council bring forward reports 9.5 Mulwala Pioneer Museum Update, 9.8 Promotional Video; and 9.9 Transgrid - Presentation to Council on the Energy Connect Project Update.
(Carried)

Live Streaming of Council Meetings
Federation Council wishes to advise members of the public that Council meetings will be recorded and will be available after each meeting on Council’s website www.federationcouncil.nsw.gov.au 
 
All care will be taken to maintain the privacy of those in attendance, however as a visitor in the public gallery, your presence may be recorded. By remaining in the public gallery, it is assumed your consent is given in the event your image is broadcast. This includes any filming by television cameras if attendance is approved by the General Manager or Mayor.

Statement of ethical obligations
Councillors are reminded of their oath or affirmation of office made under section 233A of the Act, to faithfully and impartially carry out the functions, powers, authorities and discretions vested in them under the Local Government Act 1993 or any other Act to the best of their ability and judgment, and of their obligations under Council’s Code of Conduct to disclose and appropriately manage conflicts of interest.

I ask those gathered to join us now for a few moments of silence, as we reflect on our roles in this chamber. Please use this opportunity for contemplation, prayer or thought, to focus on our shared intentions to work respectfully together for the wellbeing of our whole community.

THAT Council bring forward report 9.1 Code of Meeting Practice - Recission Motion.

179/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Patrick Bourke
  1. THAT Council note the report on the Disallowance motion passed by the NSW Parliament that no longer allows the 2025 Model Code of Meeting Practice for NSW Councils.
  2. THAT Council rescind resolution 401/2025FC, that adopted Councils current Code of Meeting Practice at the December 2025 Council meeting;
  3. THAT Council adopts Code of Meeting Practice V11 (16/21921) as tabled, which is consistent with the 2021 Code, with the minor change of:
    1. adopting clause 3.2 being - The Council shall, by resolution, set the frequency, time, date and place of its ordinary meetings, and not adopting 3.1 where the meetings are set in the Code, not allowing for flexibility, and
    2. adopting clause 8.1 being 'At a meeting of the Council, the general order of business is as fixed by resolution of the Council' and not 8.2 that sets the order of business as per the Code, not allowing for flexibility. 
  4. THAT Council rescind resolution 106/2026FC from the April 2026 Council meeting, which amended the Council adopted 2025 Code, that allowed the number of speakers apply to speak ‘for’ or ‘against’ any item of business, to be increased by the general manager or their delegate may, in consultation with the mayor or the mayor’s nominated chairperson, and allowed a Councillor to move a procedural motion that a multi-part motion consisting of several items be considered seriatim (item-by-item), and incorporate these into the new 2026 Code when adopted;
  5. THAT Council endorse the order of business being as per the current agenda format for this meeting, unless/until changed by a future Council resolution;
  6. THAT Council set the date, time, location and frequency of the following years Council meetings by resolution, at a meeting prior to the end of the preceding calendar year; and
  7. THAT Council endorse the minor changes as proposed in 4. and 5. are not substantial requiring any public exhibition, as allowed under section 362(2) of the NSW Local Government Act 1993.
(Carried)

  1. THAT Council receives and notes the report regarding Council's draft Operational Plan and Annual Budget 2026/27;
  2. THAT Council considers the request for limiting the general rate increase to the rate peg (refer to Future Federation 2026-2027 Written Community Submissions - Respondent 4 attachment) and determines that no changes be made to the 2026/27 plans, given the proposed 11.8% increase is to be invested in roads, drainage and buildings, consistent with Council's previous commitments to the community, the recent Special Rate Variation application and the IPART approval;
  3. THAT Council endorses the draft planned budget as the budget for 2026/27, inclusive of the 11.8% increase to general rates approved by IPART and the recommended changes for fuel and payroll tax expenditure budgets;

  5.   6. THAT Council publishes the Operational Plan & Annual Budget 2026/27 on Council's website within 28 days of formal adoption.

Item 9.4 Integrated Planning & Reporting Documents: Revenue Policy
Alternative motion
The below part motion was MOVED on the motion of Councillor David Bott, however on advice from the General Manager it was withdrawn to allow the report to be considered later in the meeting. The advice was that the alternative motion needed to be worded and include all appropriate and required calculations based on 50/38/12, to allow, if successful, rates to be lawfully levied. As the Councillor did not have this available, and this was not an option staff had in the report, and therefore had not calculated, staff advised that calculations could be done but this would take some time and Council may wish to defer this item until a later part of the meeting, until this was available.
 
Alternative part motion moved by Councillor David Bott
THAT Council adopt a rating structure of 50/38/12 for the final Revenue Policy 2026/27.

RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and Susan Wearne
THAT Council defer item 9.4 Integrated Planning & Reporting Documents: Revenue Policy to later in the meeting to allow staff time to provide information on these proposed amendment changes.
(Carried)

199/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Susan Wearne and David Harrison
  1. THAT Council receive and note the report and the attached Corowa - Howlong - Rutherglen On Demand Public Transport Service Proposal submitted by Matthew Kane of Regional Buses;
  2. THAT Council endorse in principle the establishment of the proposed regional on-demand public transport service as a vital link to address social isolation, economic connectivity, and public transport deficiencies within the Federation Council Local Government Area (LGA);
  3. THAT Council approve the lodgement of a formal submission to the NSW Government for the Riverina Murray Strategic Regional Integrated Transport Plan to advocate for the inclusion of this corridor;
  4. THAT Council formally advocate to the NSW Minister for Regional Transport and Minister for Roads, the Hon. Jenny Aitchison MP, and Transport for NSW (TfNSW) to secure operational funding for the service, utilising the established, fare-offset funding model currently utilised by Regional Buses;
  5. THAT Council write to Indigo Shire Council (Victoria) to seek cross-border municipal collaboration and joint advocacy, with the view of further escalating the proposal to the NSW and Victorian Cross-Border Commissioners to maximise mutual economic and social benefits; and
  6. THAT Council authorise Council officers to assist the proponent in engaging with local community networks, healthcare providers, and community groups to further document and map localised transport demand.
(Carried)

If no valid applications are received the event location will revert to the standard rotation cycle, with Mulwala and then Howlong hosting the next celebrations;

250/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and David Bott

1. THAT Council rescind the following motions carried at the 10 March 2026 Extraordinary Council meeting -

61/2026FC    5.2 Corowa Aerodrome Service Review

  1. THAT Council establish a formal ‘Aerodrome Advisory Committee’ to lead the strategic divestment of the Corowa Aerodrome to a suitably qualified private entity who is willing to acquire and assume full responsibility for its ownership on or before 30 June 2029. This includes operation, maintenance, renewal, regulatory compliance and all associated risks and liabilities, with no ongoing financial or operational obligation remaining with Federation Council.

62/2026FC    5.2 Corowa Aerodrome Service Review

  1. THAT the committee shall comprise a diverse range of stakeholders, including aviation specialists, active airport users, local business representatives, the Corowa Business Chamber, council staff and elected councillors, who shall provide regular progress reports to Council.

63/2026FC    5.2 Corowa Aerodrome Service Review

  1. THAT pending the Aerodrome Advisory Committee’s divestment outcome, Council will continue aerodrome operations with a revised fee structure. Effective 1 July 2026, occupancy/service charges will rise to $1,760 (68% increase) followed by 5% yearly increases. Further, the Council will introduce a $21,800 annual commercial rate for the site operator and a continued $19,816 ADF commitment.
2. THAT Council note the finalised Corowa Aerodrome Advisory Committee Terms of Reference with additional updates to points 3.3 and 3.4 as agreed.
(Carried)

258/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Susan Wearne and Derek Schoen
  1. THAT Council receive and note the minutes of the Lowe Square Management Committee (26/29367) held 1 June 2026;
  2. THAT Council note and endorse -
    1. Dog park irrigation - update to be finalised by spring.
    2. Design need for pedestrian access between netball courts and main oval. Lowe square committee to have survey re drainage and plan pedestrian path completed. Presented to Council and added to Lowe Square Master Plan.
  3. THAT Council endorse in principle the Lowe Square Ovals Remediation Plan prepared by the Chair of the Committee, endorsed by the Committee, and the following recommended actions, with staff to advise on any issues and progress via Committee meetings and for action updates to be recorded in Committee minutes -
    1. Recommendation: Conduct a professional irrigation audit at the start of the season to ensure every sprinkler (height, radius, and arc) is functioning optimally.
    2. Recommendation: Reinstate a strict watering target of 25mm per week, which has historically proven effective for the Hybrid Kikuyu variety.
    3. Recommendation: Transition back to conventional soil testing at a depth of 150mm to 200mm to accurately assess chemical imbalances.
    4. Recommendation: Apply soil conditioners such as Trugyp (6ton/Ha) to offset sodium and Drop Zone (2-4 lts/Ha) to lower pH levels.
    5. Recommendation: Engage Nuturf (or a similar industry leader) to provide expert guidance on soil health.
    6. Recommendation: Move to a conventional fertiliser program as recommended by Nuturf to ensure better nutrient uptake and cost efficiency.
    7. Recommendation: Formally re-evaluate the use of the bore for the football and cricket ovals to reduce reliance on expensive town water.
    8. Recommendation: Improve drainage and soil structure through vertidraining combined with a light top-dressing of sand.
    9. Recommendation: Maintain a consistent mowing height of 15mm year round.
    10. Recommendation: Utilise the Amizone mower for functional height maintenance, utilising reel mowers infrequently for final visual presentation.
    11. Recommendation: Ensure the Little Athletics track is included in the standardised mowing schedule to prevent excessive length.
    12. Recommendation: Scarifying both ovals and little athletics area twice per year during growing season.
(Carried)

This includes any filming by television cameras if attendance is approved by the General Manager or Mayor.

Statement of ethical obligations
Councillors are reminded of their oath or affirmation of office made under section 233A of the Act, to faithfully and impartially carry out the functions, powers, authorities and discretions vested in them under the Local Government Act 1993 or any other Act to the best of their ability and judgment, and of their obligations under Council’s Code of Conduct to disclose and appropriately manage conflicts of interest.

I ask those gathered to join us now for a few moments of silence, as we reflect on our roles in this chamber. Please use this opportunity for contemplation, prayer or thought, to focus on our shared intentions to work respectfully together for the wellbeing of our whole community.

270/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Bott and Andrew Kennedy
  1. THAT Council approve Development Application DA2026/86 (PAN 640151) for a two (2) lot residential subdivision at 294–296 Honour Avenue, Corowa (Lot 2 DP156532), pursuant to Section 4.16(1)(a) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, subject to standard operational and engineering conditions;
  2. THAT Council accept the written request submitted pursuant to Clause 4.6 of the Corowa Local Environmental Plan 2012 to vary the development standard under Clause 4.1 (Minimum Subdivision Lot Size), being satisfied that:
    1. Strict compliance with the 250-hectare minimum lot size standard is unreasonable and unnecessary in the circumstances of the case, as the low-impact boundary reconfiguration successfully achieves the underlying objectives of both the R1 General Residential and C3 Environmental Management zones; and
    2. There are sufficient environmental planning grounds to justify the technical variation, as the proposal simply isolates two existing operational uses without fragmenting the C3 Environmental Management corridor or introducing new development entitlements.
(Carried)

271/2026FC  RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Bott and Rowena Black
  1. THAT Council endorse option 1 in this report, and makes available the full amount of water allocated under WAL6474 (1,100 ML) for JBS Pork Australia, and require it to be purchased at a mutually agreed market rate each year, with the % of entitlement to be sold, to be tied to the percentage of the allocation made each year;
  2. THAT Council continue to make the Netherby Street raw water pump station available for use by JBS Pork Australia for access to the allocation bought from Council and JBS's own allocation under a new license agreement and work collaboratively with JBS Pork Australia to share costs associated with improving the safe access for personnel at the Netherby Street raw water pump station;
  3. THAT Council seek to modify the existing raw water agreement to reflect the above changes in points 1 & 2;
  4. THAT Council endorse JBS Pork Australia being transitioned to a "Major Industry" customer under the Council Revenue Policy, with the fees for 2026/2027 set at $1.80/kL for usage, and the availability charge for the 150mm meter set at $13,643.40 for the 2026/2027 financial year;
  5. THAT Council terminate the existing treated water supply agreement by providing JBS Pork Australia with 12 months notice; 
  6. THAT Council note that the interface point for treated water between Council's assets and JBS Pork Australia's assets remains at the water meter at the water treatment plant; and
  7. THAT Council endorse that the income generated from the sale of water allocated under WAL 6474 be internally restricted within Councils Water Fund, for the purchase of future High Security Water for Town Supply purposes.
(Carried)

272/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Derek Schoen and Andrew Kennedy
  1. THAT Council note the report regarding the Corowa BESS (SSD-87041214) Developer and Infrastructure Contributions for the proposed Battery Development at Whitehead Street, Corowa;
  2. THAT Council note that the General Manager will negotiate a draft Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) and Planning Agreement (PA) to be consistent with option 2 in this report, to include the following as a minimum:
    1. upfront capital infrastructure offset of $1,402,986 (representing 1% of the $140.3M Estimated Development Cost) 
    2. 100% indemnification for Council's actual legal, planning, and technical review expenses for the life of the project and resulting development; and
    3. Leveraging statutory authority under Section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 to enforce a binding Road Maintenance Agreement backed by independent dilapidation surveys and a pavement security bond to protect Whitehead Street and Bullecourt Road.
  3. THAT once completed, the draft MOU and draft Planning Agreement be presented to Council for endorsement, in accordance with Part 7, Division 2 Planning Agreements,  of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.
(Carried)

  1. THAT Council endorse for exhibition the amended 2026-2027 Schedule of Fees and Charges for the Urana Caravan Park to the following:

  1. THAT Council endorse a tiered Cancellation Policy for Urana Caravan Park as follows: 
    • Cancellations made > 4 weeks prior to arrival: No Fee. 
    • Cancellations made 2 to 3 weeks prior to arrival: $50 Fee. 
    • Cancellations made within 7 days of arrival: Full Tariff Charged.
  2. THAT Council delegate to the General Manager to formalise and publish the new Cancellation Policy on the Urana Caravan Park website, social media pages, and booking confirmation notices prior to the 2026 spring/summer peak season; and
  3. THAT Council receive a further report at the October Council meeting to adopt the final fee structure post exhibition of the draft fees.
(Carried)

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr Cheryl Cook announced that the first order of business is the election of mayor and vacates the chair for the returning officer (General Manager) who will conduct the election.

299/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Cheryl Cook and Andrew Kennedy
  1. THAT Council note the report on the election of a Mayor, and Deputy Mayor;
  2. THAT Council endorse the election of a Deputy Mayor, and the term be for two years, based on past practice, in line with the Mayoral term;
  3. THAT Council determine the method of voting for the elections for the Mayor and Deputy Mayor, be by way of Ordinary (Secret) Ballot; and
  4. THAT the election for the Mayor and Deputy Mayor positions be conducted by the returning officer and the results communicated.
(Carried)

The returning officer advised the meeting of the method of voting.

Election of Mayor
The returning officer read out the name of the nominee (confirmation included on form that the nominee has accepted the nomination).

As there was only one nominee for the role of mayor, the returning officer declared that Councillor Cheryl Cook is elected as mayor until the September 2028 LG election.

Deputy Mayor
Two nominations were received for the position of Deputy Mayor being Councillor Rowena Black and Councillor David Bott.

The returning officer announced the names of the candidates for deputy mayor being Councillor Rowena Black and Councillor David Bott and the Chamber was shown each name on a slip of paper before depositing into the box. The first name out of the box will be written first on the tally sheet, with second name out being written second on the tally sheet.

Director Shannon drew the Deputy Mayor voting candidates out of the box to determine the order to be written on the voting cards, with Cr Black being drawn out, then being listed first on the ballot paper.

Councillors will appear on ballet paper in the following order:
Councillor Rowena Black
Councillor David Bott

The returning officer, Adrian Butler declared that Councillor David Bott has the higher number of votes and declared that Councillor Bott is elected as Deputy Mayor until the September 2028 LG election.

Mayor resumes the chair - Councillor Cheryl Cook occupied the chair.

Councillor Cook thanked the Councillors.

301/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Harrison and Susan Wearne
  1. THAT Council note the petition from Save Mulwala Action Group Inc.;
  2. THAT Council advise Save Mulwala Action Group Inc. that Council will not accept petition request 1, and not commission a second Independent Review of the 2024 Flood Study for the reasons outlined in the report, including that an Independent Review has already been completed in 2025, and that a second review is not warranted given the outcomes of the Venant Solutions Peer Review finding the original review is sound and this being accepted by Council and the NSW Government;
  3. THAT Council advise Save Mulwala Action Group Inc. that Council is complying with request 2, ensuring transparent consultation with Mulwala residents;
  4. THAT Council advise the Save Mulwala Action Group Inc. that it is not making planning decisions based on data that lacks accuracy and credibility; and
  5. THAT Council continue to liaise closely with the Murray Darling Basin Authority and Goulburn Murray Water during the remainder of the FRMS&P and beyond in regards to possible modifications to Yarrawonga Weir in order to mitigate the influence of the Weir from causing elevated flood levels as well as other possible mitigation measures such as construction of levies, management of storages and review of added freeboard in Lake Mulwala opposite Mulwala township.
(Carried)

MOVED on the motion of Councillors David Harrison and Rowena Black
  1. THAT Council note the report on the update following exhibition of the Federation Council Stormwater Servicing Plan; and
  2. THAT an implementation plan be prepared to identify how the Stormwater Servicing Plan will be implemented prior to formal adoption.

Alannah Greenwood (Manager Communications and Engagement) left the meeting at 10:31am.
Alannah Greenwood (Manager Communications and Engagement) returned to the meeting at 10:45am.

Amendment
MOVED Councillor Susan Wearne and Seconded Councillor Rowena Black
  1. THAT Council note the report on the update following exhibition of the Federation Council Stormwater Servicing Plan; and
  2. THAT an implementation plan be prepared to identify how the Stormwater Servicing Plan will be progressed.

302/2026FC RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Susan Wearne and Rowena Black
  1. THAT Council note the report on the update following exhibition of the Federation Council Stormwater Servicing Plan; and
  2. THAT an implementation plan be prepared to identify how the Stormwater Servicing Plan will be progressed.
(Carried)

Cr Bott left the chair.

Voting for Deputy Mayor
The General Manager advised he omitted to state the results of the Deputy Mayoral election by way of votes for each candidate, and advised that Councillor Bott was successful over Councillor Black, by 5 votes to 4 votes.

Adjournment of Meeting
RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors Andrew Kennedy and Derek Schoen
THAT the meeting be adjourned for morning tea at 10:58 AM.

Resumption of Meeting
RESOLVED on the motion of Councillors David Bott and Derek Schoen
THAT the meeting resumed at 11:24 AM with all Councillors present.
